akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿أَن تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ﴾, i.e. for fear that your deeds become void. It may be said: "اسْمُكِ الحائِطَ أَنْ يَمِيلَ" (… the wall lest it lean). «[Translator's note: so in the text («اسمك»); presumably «أَمْسِكِ الحائطَ», "hold the wall".]»

akhfash:13-13.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ﴾ with kasra because it is a fresh start, and he did not construe it on ﴿لِتَعَارَفُوۤاْ﴾.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُقَدِّمُوا﴾ from «قَدَّمَ» in the meaning of «تَقَدَّمَ» (to go ahead), i.e. do not go ahead with any word or deed ﴿بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ who conveys from Him, i.e. without the permission of the two ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ﴾ of your words ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ of your deeds. It was revealed concerning the dispute of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, about appointing al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis or al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Maʿbad as commander. And concerning whoever raised his voice in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ there was revealed:

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَرْفَعُوا أَصْوَاتَكُمْ﴾ when you speak ﴿فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ﴾ when he speaks ﴿وَلَا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ﴾ when you speak privately with him ﴿كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ﴾ but lower than that, out of reverence for him ﴿أَنْ تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ i.e. for fear of that, through the raising and loudness mentioned. And concerning those who used to lower their voices in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, such as Abū Bakr, ʿUmar and others, may Allah be pleased with them, there was revealed:

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أَصْوَاتَهُمْ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ﴾ tested ﴿اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ لِلتَّقْوَى﴾ i.e. so that it may become manifest from them ﴿لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ﴾ the Garden. And concerning a group who came at midday while the Prophet ﷺ was in his house, and called out to him, there was revealed:

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنَادُونَكَ مِنْ وَرَاءِ الْحُجُرَاتِ﴾ the chambers of his wives ﷺ; the plural of «حُجْرَة», which is a piece of ground enclosed by a wall and the like. Each one of them called out behind a chamber, because they did not know in which chamber he was; calling out in the manner of the Bedouins, with roughness and coarseness ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ in what they did, your exalted rank and the reverence befitting it.

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ صَبَرُوا﴾ «أَنَّهُمْ» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); and it is said it is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e. «ثَبَتَ» ("it were established") ﴿حَتَّى تَخْرُجَ إِلَيْهِمْ لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ to whoever of them repents. And it was revealed concerning al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba: the Prophet ﷺ had sent him to Banū al-Muṣṭaliq as a collector of alms, and he feared them because of a blood-feud that had been between him and them in the Jāhiliyya, so he returned and said that they had withheld the alms and intended to kill him. The Prophet ﷺ resolved to raid them, but they came, denying what he had said about them:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ﴾ a report ﴿فَتَبَيَّنُوا﴾ its truth from its falsehood; and in one reading [فَتَثَبَّتُوا], from «الثَّبَات» (verification) ﴿أَنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا﴾ a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. for fear of that ﴿بِجَهَالَةٍ﴾ a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent), i.e. being ignorant ﴿فَتُصْبِحُوا﴾ become ﴿عَلَى مَا فَعَلْتُمْ﴾ of wrong against the people ﴿نَادِمِينَ﴾. After they had returned to their land, he ﷺ sent Khālid to them, and he saw nothing among them but obedience and good, and he informed the Prophet of that.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ فِيكُمْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ﴾ so do not speak falsehood, for Allah informs him of the true state ﴿لَوْ يُطِيعُكُمْ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ﴾ that you report contrary to what actually happened, so that he would base upon it what it requires ﴿لَعَنِتُّمْ﴾ you would have sinned, not he, the sin of causing what was based [upon it] ﴿وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْإِيمَانَ وَزَيَّنَهُ﴾ made it beautiful ﴿فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْكُفْرَ وَالْفُسُوقَ وَالْعِصْيَانَ﴾ an istidrāk (correction) in terms of meaning, not wording, because those to whom faith has been made beloved, etc., have a description different from that of those mentioned before ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ﴾ in it is iltifāt (a shift) away from direct address ﴿الرَّاشِدُونَ﴾ those firm upon their religion.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a maṣdar (verbal noun) put in the accusative by its implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e. «أَفْضَلَ» (He bestowed bounty) ﴿وَنِعْمَةً﴾ from Him ﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of them ﴿حَكِيمٌ﴾ in His bestowing favour upon them.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَإِنْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ the ayah was revealed concerning an incident: the Prophet ﷺ rode a donkey and passed by Ibn Ubayy; the donkey urinated and Ibn Ubayy held his nose, so Ibn Rawāḥa said: "By Allah, the urine of his donkey smells better than your musk." Then there was fighting between the two men's peoples with hands, sandals and palm branches ﴿اقْتَتَلُوا﴾ put in the plural in view of the meaning, because each party is a group; and it was read [اقْتَتَلَا] ﴿فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا﴾ put in the dual in view of the wording ﴿فَإِنْ بَغَتْ﴾ transgressed ﴿إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَى الْأُخْرَى فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّى تَفِيءَ﴾ returns ﴿إِلَى أَمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾ the truth ﴿فَإِنْ فَاءَتْ فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا بِالْعَدْلِ﴾ with equity ﴿وَأَقْسِطُوا﴾ be just ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ﴾ in religion ﴿فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ﴾ when they quarrel; and it was read [إِخْوَتِكُمْ] with the tāʾ ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ﴾

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا يَسْخَرْ﴾ the ayah was revealed concerning the delegation of Tamīm when they mocked the poor among the Muslims, such as ʿAmmār and Ṣuhayb; mockery is disdain and contempt ﴿قَوْمٌ﴾ i.e. men among you ﴿مِنْ قَوْمٍ عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْرًا مِنْهُمْ﴾ in the sight of Allah ﴿وَلَا نِسَاءٌ﴾ among you ﴿مِنْ نِسَاءٍ عَسَى أَنْ يَكُنَّ خَيْرًا مِنْهُنَّ وَلَا تَلْمِزُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ do not find fault, lest you be found fault with, i.e. let not some of you find fault with others ﴿وَلَا تَنَابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقَابِ﴾ let not some of you call others by a nickname they dislike, and among such is "O sinner" and "O disbeliever" ﴿بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ﴾ mentioned, of mockery, fault-finding and name-calling ﴿الْفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ الْإِيمَانِ﴾ a badal (substitute) of «الِاسْمُ», because it conveys that it is iniquity, since it usually recurs ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَتُبْ﴾ from that ﴿فَأُولَئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ﴾.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ﴾ i.e. causing sin, and it is much, such as thinking ill of the people of good among the believers, and they are many; unlike thinking so of the sinners among them, for there is no sin in it regarding the like of what appears from them ﴿وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا﴾ one of the two tāʾs has been dropped from it; do not pursue the faults and failings of the Muslims by searching for them ﴿وَلَا يَغْتَبْ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا﴾ let him not mention him with something he dislikes, even if it is in him ﴿أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا﴾ with the light and the doubled [yāʾ], i.e. it does not befit him ﴿فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ﴾ i.e. backbiting him in his life is like eating his flesh after his death; the second has been put before you and you hated it, so hate the first ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ i.e. His punishment for backbiting, by repenting from it ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ﴾ accepting the repentance of those who repent ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَى﴾ Ādam and Ḥawwāʾ ﴿وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوبًا﴾ the plural of «شَعْب» with fatḥa on the shīn; it is the highest level of lineage ﴿وَقَبَائِلَ﴾ they are below the shuʿūb, and after them come the ʿamāʾir, then the buṭūn, then the afkhādh, then the faṣāʾil, the last of them. An example of it: Khuzayma is a shaʿb, Kināna a qabīla, Quraysh an ʿimāra (with kasra on the ʿayn), Quṣayy a baṭn, Hāshim a fakhdh, al-ʿAbbās a faṣīla ﴿لِتَعَارَفُوا﴾ one of the two tāʾs has been dropped from it; so that you may know one another, not so that you may boast of the loftiness of lineage; boasting is only by taqwā (God-consciousness) ﴿إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ﴾ of you ﴿خَبِيرٌ﴾ of your inner selves.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿قَالَتِ الْأَعْرَابُ﴾ a group from Banū Asad ﴿آمَنَّا﴾ we have believed with our hearts ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَلَكِنْ قُولُوا أَسْلَمْنَا﴾ i.e. we have submitted outwardly ﴿وَلَمَّا﴾ has not ﴿يَدْخُلِ الْإِيمَانُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ until now, but it is expected from you ﴿وَإِنْ تُطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ with faith and other things ﴿لَا يَأْلِتْكُمْ﴾ with the hamza and without it [لَا يَلِتْكُمْ], and by changing it into an alif; He will not diminish for you ﴿مِنْ أَعْمَالِكُمْ﴾ i.e. of their reward ﴿شَيْئًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ﴾ to the believers ﴿رَحِيمٌ﴾ to them.

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ i.e. those truthful in their faith, as is stated explicitly afterwards ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتَابُوا﴾ did not doubt in faith ﴿وَجَاهَدُوا بِأَمْوَالِهِمْ وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ so their jihad makes manifest the truthfulness of their faith ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الصَّادِقُونَ﴾ in their faith, not those who said "we have believed" and from whom nothing but submission (islām) was found.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ to them ﴿أَتُعَلِّمُونَ اللَّهَ بِدِينِكُمْ﴾ the doubled form of «عَلِمَ» in the meaning of «شَعَرَ» (to be aware), i.e. do you make Him aware of what you hold in your saying "we have believed"? ﴿وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَاللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُوا﴾ without fighting, unlike others who became Muslim after being fought among them ﴿قُلْ لَا تَمُنُّوا عَلَيَّ إِسْلَامَكُمْ﴾ accusative by removal of the preposition (bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ), the bāʾ, and it is implied before «أَنْ» in both places ﴿بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ هَدَاكُمْ لِلْإِيمَانِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾ in your saying "we have believed".

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَعْلَمُ غَيْبَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ what is hidden in them ﴿وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِمَا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تَعْمَلُونَ]; nothing of it is hidden from Him.

daas-irab:12-13.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيراً﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿مِنَ الظَّنِّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كثيرا. ﴿إِنَّ بَعْضَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿الظَّنِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (the second term of the genitive construct). ﴿إِثْمٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl). ﴿وَلا تَجَسَّسُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا يَغْتَبْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by the lā of prohibition. ﴿بَعْضُكُمْ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿بَعْضاً﴾ its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَيُحِبُّ﴾ the hamza is a particle of interrogation and rebuke, and a nominative (marfūʿ) imperfect verb. ﴿أَحَدُكُمْ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, and its mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَخِيهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ. ﴿مَيْتاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ﴾ the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (fāʾ of elucidation), and a past verb with its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is for lengthening (ishbāʿ); the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ a particle of resumption, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its two predicates; the nominal clause is an explanation of cause and has no grammatical position. ﴿يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ﴾ the i'rab of its like has preceded. ﴿إِنَّا﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿خَلَقْناكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of inna. ﴿مِنْ ذَكَرٍ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَأُنْثى﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ذكر; the nominal clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿وَجَعَلْناكُمْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first mafʿūl; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿شُعُوباً﴾ its second mafʿūl. ﴿وَقَبائِلَ﴾ conjoined to شعوبا. ﴿لِتَعارَفُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an concealed after the lām of causation, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعلناكم. ﴿إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَتْقاكُمْ﴾ the khabar of inna; the nominal clause is explanatory of cause (taʿlīliyya). ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its two predicates; the nominal clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:14-15.t: ﴿قالَتِ﴾ a past verb. ﴿الْأَعْرابُ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿آمَنَّا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ a particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿قُولُوا﴾ an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَسْلَمْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and an imperfect verb, jussive by lammā. ﴿الْإِيمانُ﴾ its fāʿil. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and in is conditional, governing the jussive. ﴿تُطِيعُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause تطيعوا is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to it. ﴿لا يَلِتْكُمْ﴾ lā is negating, and an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the kāf is its mafʿūl and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ أَعْمالِكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿شَيْئاً﴾ a second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its two predicates; the clause is an explanation of cause (taʿlīl) and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa). ﴿الْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لَمْ يَرْتابُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by lam, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَجاهَدُوا﴾ conjoined to آمنوا. ﴿بِأَمْوالِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ conjoined to أموالهم. ﴿فِي سَبِيلِ﴾ the two are also attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الصَّادِقُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:16-18.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position. ﴿أَتُعَلِّمُونَ﴾ the hamza is a particle of rebuking interrogation, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿بِدِينِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِكُلِّ﴾ the two are attached to عليم. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلِيمٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَمُنُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative. ﴿أَسْلَمُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). ﴿قُلْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿لا تَمُنُّوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lā of prohibition, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيَّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿إِسْلامَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the object of saying. ﴿بَلِ﴾ a particle of conjunction and digression (iḍrāb). ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَمُنُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to يمن. ﴿أَنْ﴾ a maṣdar-forming particle governing the accusative. ﴿هَداكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl; the fāʿil is latent. ﴿لِلْإِيمانِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition. ﴿أَنْ﴾ conditional, governing the jussive. [Translator's note: the source writes «أن» here; the Quranic word is ﴿إِنْ﴾ (in), the conditional particle.] ﴿كُنْتُمْ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb and its noun. ﴿صادِقِينَ﴾ its khabar; the verbal clause is initial and has no grammatical position, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because what precedes indicates it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿غَيْبَ﴾ its mafʿūl. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ﴾ the wāw is a particle of resumption, and a mubtadaʾ and its khabar. ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to what follows them. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, and the nominal clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:1-4.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), and hā is for drawing attention (tanbīh). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a badal (substitute) of ayyuhā. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), and the vocative clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿لا تُقَدِّمُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān). ﴿يَدَيِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَرَسُولِهِ﴾ conjoined to what came before. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (اللَّهِ); as mafʿūl bihi it is اللَّهَ.] ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ﴾ inna, its noun and its two khabars (predicates); the clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl). ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا﴾ its i'rab is like the preceding one. ﴿أَصْواتَكُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَوْقَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿صَوْتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿النَّبِيِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lā is prohibitive. ﴿تَجْهَرُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by lā, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿بِالْقَوْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to the verb. ﴿كَجَهْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿بَعْضِكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِبَعْضٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to jahr. ﴿أَنْ تَحْبَطَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an. ﴿أَعْمالُكُمْ﴾ fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by annexation to an omitted mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿وَأَنْتُمْ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿تَشْعُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يَغُضُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَصْواتَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عِنْدَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿رَسُولِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the nominal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause inna is resumptive. ﴿امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil. ﴿قُلُوبَهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لِلتَّقْوى﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila of alladhīna. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿مَغْفِرَةٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿وَأَجْرٌ﴾ conjoined to maghfira. ﴿عَظِيمٌ﴾ an adjective; the nominal clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يُنادُونَكَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is its fāʿil and the kāf a mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿مِنْ وَراءِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْحُجُراتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, the nominal clause is the khabar of inna, and the clause inna is resumptive.

daas-irab:5-7.t: ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and law is a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿صَبَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from anna and what follows it is in the position of the nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb. ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive. ﴿تَخْرُجَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after ḥattā. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the interpreted maṣdar from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ṣabarū. ﴿لَكانَ﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of law. ﴿كان﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿خَيْراً﴾ its khabar, and the noun of kāna is latent (mustatir). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to khayran; the verbal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its two khabars; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿إِنْ﴾ a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿جاءَكُمْ﴾ a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the kāf is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فاسِقٌ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِنَبَإٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿فَتَبَيَّنُوا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿أَنْ تُصِيبُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative by an, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿قَوْماً﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar from an and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by annexation to an omitted mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), the implied form being "out of dislike of your striking" (karāhata iṣābatikum). ﴿بِجَهالَةٍ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَتُصْبِحُوا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a defective imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its noun. ﴿عَلى ما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to nādimīn. ﴿فَعَلْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of mā. ﴿نادِمِينَ﴾ khabar, accusative by the yāʾ. ﴿وَاعْلَمُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿أَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿فِيكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. ﴿رَسُولَ﴾ the postponed noun of anna. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the interpreted maṣdar from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of iʿlamū. ﴿لَوْ﴾ a conditional particle that does not cause the jussive. ﴿يُطِيعُكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is initial and has no grammatical position. ﴿فِي كَثِيرٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿مِنَ الْأَمْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to kathīr. ﴿لَعَنِتُّمْ﴾ the lām falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَلكِنَّ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and lākinna is a particle resembling the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its noun. [Translator's note: the source prints the word with a kasra (اللَّهِ); as the noun of lākinna it is اللَّهَ.] ﴿حَبَّبَ﴾ a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, and the clause is the khabar of lākinna. ﴿إِلَيْكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْإِيمانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَزَيَّنَهُ﴾ conjoined to ḥabbaba. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَكَرَّهَ﴾ conjoined to zayyana. ﴿إِلَيْكُمُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿الْكُفْرَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَالْفُسُوقَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَالْعِصْيانَ﴾ conjoined to what came before. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الرَّاشِدُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive.

daas-irab:8-10.t: ﴿فَضْلًا﴾ mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) faḍlan. ﴿وَنِعْمَةً﴾ conjoined to faḍlan. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ﴾ two khabars (predicates); the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and in is conditional. ﴿طائِفَتانِ﴾ the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the alif. ﴿مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of ṭāʾifatān. ﴿اقْتَتَلُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is explicative (tafsīriyya), and the omitted protasis clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿فَأَصْلِحُوا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place (ẓarf makān); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿فَإِنْ بَغَتْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, in is conditional, and a past verb. ﴿إِحْداهُما﴾ fāʿil. ﴿عَلَى الْأُخْرى﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is initial. ﴿فَقاتِلُوا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿الَّتِي﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿تَبْغِي﴾ an imperfect verb; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿حَتَّى تَفِيءَ﴾ a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive, and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implicit an after ḥattā, its fāʿil latent. ﴿إِلى أَمْرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and the verb is in the position of the genitive by ḥattā, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to qātilū. ﴿فَإِنْ﴾ a conjunction, and in is a conditional particle causing the jussive. ﴿فاءَتْ﴾ a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). ﴿فَأَصْلِحُوا﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis, and an imperative verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis. ﴿بَيْنَهُما﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿بِالْعَدْلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿وَأَقْسِطُوا﴾ conjoined to aṣliḥū. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, with its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation (taʿlīl). ﴿إِنَّمَا﴾ a restraining particle and the restrained one (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَأَصْلِحُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb of place. ﴿أَخَوَيْكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ; the clause is the apodosis of a condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its object. ﴿لَعَلَّكُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun. ﴿تُرْحَمُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the khabar of laʿalla, and the nominal clause is a causal explanation.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿لا يَسْخَرْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā. ﴿قَوْمٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿مِنْ قَوْمٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿عَسى﴾ a complete (tāmm) past verb. ﴿أَنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْراً﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an; the wāw is its noun and khayran its khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to khayran; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from an and what follows it is the fāʿil of ʿasā. ﴿وَلا نِساءٌ مِنْ نِساءٍ عَسى أَنْ يَكُنَّ خَيْراً مِنْهُنَّ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it, and the clause ʿasā is resumptive. ﴿وَلا تَلْمِزُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive lā; the wāw is its fāʿil and anfusakum its object. ﴿وَلا تَنابَزُوا﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿بِالْأَلْقابِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb. ﴿بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ﴾ an invariable (jāmid) past verb of blame (dhamm), and its fāʿil. ﴿الْفُسُوقُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause biʾsa is its khabar. ﴿بَعْدَ﴾ an adverb of time (ẓarf zamān). ﴿الْإِيمانِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and man is a conditional noun causing the jussive, a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لَمْ يَتُبْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive by lam, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), with its fāʿil latent (mustatir). ﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾ the fāʾ falls in the apodosis of the condition, and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الظَّالِمُونَ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the two clauses of the protasis and the apodosis are the khabar, and the clause man is resumptive.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ لاَ تُقَدِّمُواْ﴾.
The readers agreed on it; and had a reader read (لا تَقْدَموا), it would have been correct. One says: "I went forward (qadamtu) in such-and-such" and "I went ahead (taqaddamtu)".

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لاَ تَرْفَعُوۤاْ أَصْوَاتَكُمْ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "بأصواتكم". Like it in speech: "He spoke fine speech" and "He spoke with fine speech".
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَجْهَرُواْ لَهُ بِٱلْقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ.﴾: he says: do not say "O Muḥammad", but say: "O Prophet of Allah, O Messenger of Allah, O Abū al-Qāsim".
His saying: ﴿أَن تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ﴾.
Its meaning is: lest (لا) [your deeds] come to naught; and in it the jussive and the nominative [are possible] if you put (لا) in place of (أن); and it has been explained in more than one place. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: فتحبطَ أعمالكم, and that is evidence for the permissibility of the jussive in it.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying: ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱمْتَحَنَ ٱللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ﴾.
He purified them for piety, as gold is tested with fire, so its good part comes out and its dross falls away.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿مِن وَرَآءِ ٱلْحُجُرَاتِ﴾.
The [usual] way of speech is to give the ḥāʾ and the jīm ḍamma; and some of the Arabs say: الْحُجَرات and الرُّكَبات, and every plural that is said, for three to ten, as ghuraf and ḥujar: when you pluralize it with tāʾ, you give its second [letter] fatḥa. But the ḍamma [180/b] is better than that.
His saying: ﴿أَكْثَرُهُمْ لاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
The delegation of the Banū Tamīm came to him at midday while he, Allah bless him, was asleep, and they began calling: "O Muḥammad, come out to us!" He woke and came out, and there was revealed: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُنَادُونَكَ مِن وَرَآءِ ٱلْحُجُرَاتِ﴾ to the end of the verse. After that he gave them leave; their poet and the poet of the Muslims stood up, and an orator of theirs and the orator of the Muslims, and their voices rose in boasting. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down concerning it: ﴿لاَ تَرْفَعُوۤاْ أَصْوَاتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ ٱلنَّبِيِّ﴾.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِن جَآءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتثَبّتُوا﴾.
[This is] the reading of the companions of ʿAbd Allāh, and I saw it in the codex of ʿAbd Allāh with thāʾ; and the reading of the people is (فَتَبَيَّنُوا), and their meanings are close, because His saying (فَتَبَيَّنُوا) means: wait until you know, and that is the meaning of تثبتوا. That was only because the Prophet, Allah bless him, sent an agent to the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq to take their alms. When he headed towards them, they came out to meet him to honour him, and he thought they intended to fight him. So he returned to the Prophet, Allah bless him, and said: "They fought me and refused me payment of what they owe." While they were in that state, and the Prophet, Allah bless him, had become angry, the delegation of the Banū al-Muṣṭaliq came to him and said: "We wanted to honour the envoy of the Messenger of Allah and to pay the due to him." The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him, suspected them and did not believe them; so Allah sent down: "ياأَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ إِن جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَثَبّتُوا" to the end of the verse, and the verse after it.

farraa:9-10.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِن طَآئِفَتَانِ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ ٱقْتَتَلُواْ﴾.
He did not say اقتتلتا (dual). In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: فخذوا بينهم, in place of فأصلحوا بينهم; and in his reading: حتى يَفِيئُوا إلى أمر الله فإن فاءوا فخذوا بينهم.
His saying: ﴿فَأَصْلِحُواْ بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ﴾.
He did not say بين إخوتكم or إخوانكم; and had that been said, it would have been correct.
It was revealed concerning the clan of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy and the clan of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥa al-Anṣārī. The Messenger of Allah, Allah bless him, passed on a donkey and stopped by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ubayy in the gathering of his people. The donkey of the Messenger of Allah dropped dung, and ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Ubayy] put his hand over his nose and said: "Keep your donkey away; it has annoyed me." Ibn Rawāḥa said to him: "Do you say this of the donkey of the Messenger of Allah? By Allah, it is of better repute than you and your father." The people of this one and the people of that one grew angry, until they fought with hands and sandals; so this verse was revealed.
His saying: ﴿فَقَاتِلُواْ ٱلَّتِي تَبْغِي﴾: the one that does not accept reconciliation. And the Prophet, Allah bless him, reconciled them.

farraa:11-13.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ﴾.
It was revealed because Thābit ibn Qays al-Anṣārī was hard of hearing, and he used to draw near the Prophet, Allah bless him, to hear his speech. He came after one rakʿa of the dawn prayer had been completed, when the people had taken their places near the Messenger of Allah. He began stepping over [them] and saying: "Make room," until he reached a man just short of the Prophet, Allah bless him, and said: "Make room." The man said to him: "You have found a place, so sit." When it became light, he said: "Who is the man?" He said: "So-and-so son of so-and-so." He said: "You are the son of such-and-such a woman", [naming] a mother of his for whom he used to be reproached. That grieved the man, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down: ﴿لاَ يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِّن قَوْمٍ عَسَىٰ أَن يَكُونُواْ خَيْراً مِّنْهُمْ﴾. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, as far as I know, it is: عَسَوا أن يكونوا خيراً منهم ولا نساء من نساء عسَين أن يكنَّ خيراً منهن.
And there was also revealed concerning this story: [181/a] ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوباً﴾. The shuʿūb (peoples) are larger than the tribes, and the tribes are larger than the clans (afkhādh). ﴿لِتَعَارَفُوۤاْ﴾: that you may know one another in lineage. ﴿إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ﴾ has kasra; the verb تعارف does not fall on it; and it is the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: لتعارفوا بينكم وخيركم عند الله أتقاكم. Thābit said: "By Allah, I will never vie with any man in his lineage again."
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَلْمِزُوۤاْ أَنفُسَكُمْ﴾.
Let not some of you find fault with others; "and do not insult one another with nicknames": a man would say to a man of the Jews who had embraced Islam: "O Jew!", so they were forbidden that; and He said concerning it: ﴿بِئْسَ ٱلاسْمُ ٱلْفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ ٱلإَيمَانِ﴾. And whoever gives fatḥa: أن أكرمكم, it is as though he said: "that you may know one another [in] that the noble one is the pious". Had it been so, it would have been لتعرفوا أن أكرمكم; but لتعارفوا is allowed [in the sense]: that some of you may make known to others that the noblest of you with Allah is the most pious of you.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَجَسَّسُواْ﴾.
The readers are agreed on the jīm. It was revealed specifically about Salmān; they had spoken ill of him.
His saying: ﴿فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ﴾.
The Prophet, Allah bless him, said to them: "Would any of you eat the flesh of his brother after his death?" They said: "No!" He said: "Backbiting is eating his flesh." It is that you say what is in him; and when you say what is not in him, that is slander (al-baht), not backbiting. "So you would hate it", i.e. you have hated it, so do not do it.
And whoever reads فكُرِّهتموه says: it has been made hateful to you; and the meaning, and Allah knows best, is one; and it is in the position of your saying: "The man died (māta)" and "was caused to die (umīta)".

farraa:14-17.t:
His saying: ﴿قَالَتِ ٱلأَعْرَابُ آمَنَّا قُل لَّمْ تُؤْمِنُواْ وَلَـٰكِن قُولُوۤاْ أَسْلَمْنَا﴾.
This was revealed concerning the Bedouins of the Banū Asad. They came to the Prophet, Allah bless him and grant him peace, at Medina with their families, desiring alms, and they kept coming in the evening and the morning, saying: "Give to us, for we have come to you with families and baggage, while the Arabs came to you on the backs of their mounts." So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent down: ﴿يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُواْ﴾. (أن) is in the position of the accusative, because in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: يمنون عليك إسلامهم. And had you made it: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْك لأنْ أَسْلَمُوا ("because they submitted"), then when you drop the lām it is an accusative different from the first accusative.
His saying: ﴿أَنْ هَداكُمْ﴾; and in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: إذ هداكم.
So (أن) is in the position of the accusative, not by the verb falling on it but by the dropping of the preposition (al-ṣifa).
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَلِتْكُمْ﴾.
He will not diminish you, nor wrong you in anything of your deeds. It is from lāta, yalītu, and the readers are agreed on it. Some read: لا يَأْلِتْكم, but I do not like it, because it was written in the codices without alif, and this is not a position where dropping the hamza is allowed. Do you not see His saying (يأتون), (يأمرون) and (يأكلون): the alif was not dropped in any of them, because it is vowelless; the hamza is dropped only when what precedes it is vowelless, but when it itself, meaning the hamza, is vowelless, it remains and is not dropped. He ventured to read it "يألتكم" only because he found ﴿وَمَا أَلَتْنَاهُمْ مِنْ عَمَلِهِمْ مِنْ شَيْءٍ﴾ in one place, and took this from that. The Qurʾān brings both differing dialects. Do you not see His saying: ﴿تُمْلَىٰ عَلَيْهِ﴾, while in another place it is: ﴿فَلْيَكْتُبْ وَلْيُمْلِل﴾, and one was not made to conform to the other so that they agree? Lāta yalītu and alata yaʾlitu are two dialects. [He said: Muḥammad ibn al-Jahm ibn Ibrāhīm al-Simmarī narrated to us, saying: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us.]

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «الذين»: ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). The clause «واتقوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «لا تُقَدِّموا».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The preposition «كجهر»: the kāf stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "a raising of the voice like the raising of …"; the preposition «لبعض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the maṣdar (verbal noun) (جهر). The maṣdar «أن تحبط» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for fear that"; the clause «وأنتم لا تشعرون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «أولئك الذين» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ»; the clause «لهم مغفرة» is a second khabar of «إنّ».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The clause «أكثرهم لا يعقلون» is the khabar (predicate) of «إنّ».

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The conditional clause is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause {إِنَّ الَّذِينَ}. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from «أنَّ» and what follows it is the fāʿil (agent) of «ثبت» [Translator's note: an implied verb, i.e. "had it been established that …"]. The noun (ism) of «كان» refers to the pronoun understood from «صبروا», i.e. "the patience would have been". The preposition «لهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «خيرا».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, the response to the vocative; the maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن تصيبوا» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "for fear that".

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The clause «واعلموا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the preceding conditional clause; the conditional clause «لو يطيعكم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «فيكم»; the preposition «من الأمر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كثير». The clause «ولكن الله حبَّب» is conjoined to the clause «يطيعكم»; «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), and the clause «أولئك هم الراشدون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: «فضلا» stands in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. "He bestowed a bounty"; the preposition «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «فضلا».

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «طائفتان» is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb explained by what follows it, and the clause «اقتتلوا» is explicative. The clause «فإن بَغَتْ» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause, and the clause «فإن فاءت» is conjoined to the clause «بَغَتْ».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: The clause «فأصلحوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause «إنما المؤمنون إخوة», and the clause «لعلكم ترحمون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The clause «لا يسخر» is the response to the vocative, resumptive; the preposition «من قوم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يسخر». The clause «عسى أن يكونوا» is resumptive; «أن» and what follows it is the fāʿil (agent) of the complete (tāmma) «عسى»; the preposition «منهم» is attached to «خيرا». His words «ولا نساء»: a noun maʿṭūf (conjoined) to «قوم»; the preposition «من نساء» is conjoined to «من قوم» and attached to what that is attached to. The clause «عسى أن يكنَّ» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يكنَّ» is the fāʿil of «عسى». The clause «بئس الاسم» is resumptive: a past verb and its fāʿil; «الفسوق» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it is wickedness", and the clause (هو الفسوق) is explicative of «الاسم». The adverb «بعد» is attached to the maṣdar (الفسوق). The clause «ومن لم يتب» is resumptive, and «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: «كثيرا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the preposition «من الظن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «كثيرا». The clause «أيحب أحدكم» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is a mafʿūl bihi; «ميتا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أخيه». The clause «فكرهتموه» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to an omitted verb, its implied form being "that was put to you and you abhorred it", and the clause (عرض) is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: «شعوبا» is the second object; the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «لتعارفوا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعلناكم»; the adverb «عند» is attached to «أكرمكم».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The clause «قل» is resumptive; the clause «ولكن قولوا» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause «لم تؤمنوا»; the clause «ولما يدخل» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «وإن تطيعوا» is conjoined to the clause «لم تؤمنوا»; «شيئا» is the second object.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: «الذين» is the khabar (predicate) of «المؤمنون»; «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); the clause «أولئك الصادقون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «والله يعلم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause «والله عليم» is resumptive; the preposition «بكل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «عليم».

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن أسلموا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). The clause «بل الله يَمُنُّ» is resumptive, and the maṣdar «أن هداكم» is a mafʿūl bihi. The clause «إن كنتم صادقين» is resumptive; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: The clause «والله بصير» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the resumptive clause «إن الله يعلم»; the preposition «بما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بصير».

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying, Exalted is He, {كجهر بَعْضكُم لبَعض}: the كاف is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "a loudness like the loudness" (جهرا كجهر).
His saying {أَن تحبط أَعمالكُم}: أن is in the position of the accusative by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "lest your deeds be nullified" (لأن تحبط), like {رَبنَا ليضلوا عَن سَبِيلك}.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying {إِن الَّذين يَغُضُّونَ أَصْوَاتهم}: the khabar (predicate) of إنّ is أُولَئِكَ الَّذين. It is also said that it [أولئك الذين] is a naʿt (adjective) of الذين, and the khabar is لهم مغفرة وأجر عظيم, which is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the position of the khabar of إنّ.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying إِن الَّذين يُنَادُونَك: the khabar (predicate) of إنّ is أكثرهم لا يعقلون, which is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar in the position of the khabar of إنّ. In ordinary speech, أكثرَهم in the accusative is permissible as a badal (substitute) of الذين, and it is the badal of a thing where the second is a part of it.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t:
His saying وَإِن طَائِفَتَانِ: طائفتان is nominative by an implied verb, its implied form being "and if two parties fight" (وإن اقتتل طائفتان) or "and if there are two parties" (وإن كان طائفتان), because إنْ is for condition, and a condition can only be with a verb, so a verb had to be implied. It is like وَإِن أحد من الْمُشْركين. It is not permissible to omit the verb with any of the governing conditional particles except with إنْ alone, and that is because of its strength and because it is the root of the conditional particles.
His saying أَن تصيبوا: أن is in the position of the accusative because it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), and فتصبحوا is conjoined to it.

mekki-muskil:14-14.t:
His saying {قل لم تؤمنوا}: لم came, and لن did not come, because it is a negation of what is past, while لن is only a negation of what is to come. The people only reported about themselves a faith that had already taken place, so Allah the Exalted negated their claim with لم. Had they reported about themselves a faith that would come to be, the negation would have been with لن. Do you not see His saying, Exalted is He, فاستأذنوك للخروج فقل لن تخرجوا معي أبدا? That is because they only said "We will go out with you, O Muhammad", asking permission for a going-out yet to begin; therefore it was negated with لن and not with لم.
His saying {لَا يلتكم من أَعمالكُم}: whoever reads it with a lām after the yāʾ takes it from لات يليت, like كال يكيل; and whoever reads it with a hamza after the yāʾ takes it from ألت يألت. In this there are two dialects: one of them is ألت يألت, and the majority read with it in Sūrat al-Ṭūr وما ألتناهم; and the other dialect is ألت يألت, and Ibn Kathīr read with it in Sūrat al-Ṭūr وما ألتناهم. [Translator's note: the two dialects are written identically here in the edition; they are presumably meant to differ in vowelling (e.g. أَلَتَ يَأْلِتُ versus أَلِتَ يَأْلَتُ), which would account for Ibn Kathīr's وما أَلِتْناهم.] All of it means diminishing.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا: a vocative particle for one at middle distance; ﴿أي﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين: an adjective of ﴿أي﴾; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿لا تقدموا بين يدي الله ورسوله﴾: لا: prohibitive; تقدموا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). There are [two views] about it: [first,] that it is transitive and its object has been omitted to convey generality, or the object has been left out in order to focus on the action itself, as in their saying: "he gives and withholds"; the second: that it is intransitive, like وجّه and توجّه. بين: a mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تقدموا﴾; يدي الله: muḍāf ilayhi, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ in place of the kasra, because it is a dual; the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi; رسوله is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty.
﴿واتقوا الله إن الله سميع عليم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; اتقوا: an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the Name of Majesty is its noun; سميع: its khabar (predicate); عليم: its second khabar; the clause is causal (taʿlīliyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿إنما المؤمنون إخوة فأصلحوا بين أخويكم﴾: إنما: [إنّ] made inoperative (makfūfa) by the preventing [mā] (kāffa); المؤمنون: mubtadaʾ (subject); إخوة: khabar (predicate); فأصلحوا: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition); أصلحوا: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); بين أخويكم: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أصلحوا﴾.
﴿واتقوا الله لعلكم ترحمون﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes; لعل: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh) expressing hope; ﴿كم﴾: its noun; the clause ترحمون is its khabar.

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا: a vocative particle; ﴿أي﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين: an adjective of ﴿أي﴾; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿لا يسخر قوم من قوم عسى أن يكونوا خيرا منهم﴾: لا: prohibitive; يسخر: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا; قوم: fāʿil (agent); من قوم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يسخر﴾; عسى: a past verb, one of the verbs of hope, and here it is complete (tāmma); ﴿أنْ﴾ is maṣdariyya (infinitival); يكونوا: a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw of the group is the noun of يكون; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يكونوا﴾ is the fāʿil of عسى; خيرًا: the khabar (predicate) of يكون; منهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خيرا﴾; the clause ﴿عسى أن يكونوا...﴾ is resumptive, giving the reason for the prohibition, with no grammatical position.
﴿ولا نساء من نساء﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لا﴾: prohibitive; نساء: the fāʿil of an omitted verb, i.e. ولا يسخرْ نساءٌ من نساء ("nor let women mock women"); ﴿من نساء﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the implied verb ﴿يسخر﴾; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿لا يسخر قوم من قوم﴾.
﴿عسى أن يكن خيرًا منهن﴾: عسى: a past verb, one of the verbs of hope, and here it is complete (tāmma); ﴿أنْ﴾ is maṣdariyya; يكنَّ: a defective imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn in the position of accusative; the wāw was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the nūn of the feminine plural (nūn al-niswa) is the noun of يكون; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يكنَّ﴾ is the fāʿil of عسى; خيرًا: the khabar of يكون; منهنَّ: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿خيرا﴾; the clause ﴿عسى أن يكنَّ...﴾ is resumptive, giving the reason for the prohibition, with no grammatical position.
﴿ولا تلمزوا أنفسكم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لا﴾: prohibitive; تلمزوا: an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw of the group is the fāʿil; أنفسكم: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the attached pronoun is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿ولا تلمزوا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿لا يسخر قوم من قوم﴾.
﴿ولا تنابزوا بالألقاب﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿لا﴾: prohibitive; تنابزوا: an imperfect verb, jussive by the prohibitive لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw of the group is the fāʿil; بالألقاب: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تنابزوا﴾; the clause ﴿ولا تنابزوا﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿لا يسخر قوم من قوم﴾.
﴿بئس الاسم الفسوق بعد الإيمان﴾: بئس: a past, inflexible (jāmid) verb for expressing blame; الاسم: its fāʿil; الفسوق: the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm); it is a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar is the clause before it, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; بعد الإيمان: the adverb is attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿ومن لم يتب فأولئك هم الظالمون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; من: a jussive conditional noun; لم: a particle of negation, of conversion [to past meaning] and of the jussive; يتب: an imperfect verb, jussive by لم, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ links the apodosis, because it is a nominal clause; أولئك: mubtadaʾ; هم: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position, or a second mubtadaʾ; الظالمون: the khabar of من [Translator's note: so in the source; presumably the khabar of أولئك is meant], or the khabar of هم, and the clause is the khabar of أولئك; the clause فأولئك is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا: a vocative particle; ﴿أي﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين: an adjective of ﴿أي﴾; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿اجتنبوا كثيرا من الظن إن بعض الظن إثم﴾: اجتنبوا: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); كثيرًا: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من الظن: an adjective of ﴿كثيرًا﴾; إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); بعض: its noun; الظن: muḍāf ilayhi; إثم: its khabar (predicate); إن with what falls within its scope gives the reason for the prohibition, so the clause has no grammatical position.
﴿ولا تجسسوا ولا يغتب بعضكم بعضا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; لا: prohibitive; تجسسوا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; ولا يغتب is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ولا تجسسوا; بعضكم: fāʿil; بعضًا: mafʿūl bihi.
﴿أيحب أحدكم أن يأكل لحم أخيه ميتا فكرهتموه﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (taqrīrī); يحب: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); أحدكم: fāʿil; أن with what falls within its scope is the object of يحب; ميتًا: a ḥāl (circumstantial) from لحم أخيه, or from الأخ; the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition); كرهتموه: a verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; the wāw is for lengthening (ishbāʿ) the ḍamma of the mīm.
﴿واتقوا الله إن الله تواب رحيم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; اتقوا الله: an imperative verb, its fāʿil and a mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿واتقوا الله﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position; إن: an abrogating particle; the Name of Majesty is its noun; تواب: its khabar; رحيم: its second khabar.

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿يا أيها الناس﴾: يا: a vocative particle; ﴿أي﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الناس: an adjective of ﴿أي﴾.
﴿إنا خلقناكم من ذكر وأنثى﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿نا﴾: its noun; the clause خلقناكم is its khabar (predicate); من ذكر: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) خلقناكم; أنثى is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ذكر.
﴿وجعلناكم شعوبًا وقبائل لتعارفوا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; جعلناكم: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); شعوبًا: the second mafʿūl bihi; the lām is causal (taʿlīl); تعارفوا: an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām of cause; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to جعلناكم.
﴿إن أكرمكم عند الله أتقاكم إن الله عليم خبير﴾: إن: an abrogating particle; أكرمكم: its noun; عند الله: an adverb attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); أتقاكم: the khabar of إن; إن: an abrogating particle; the Name of Majesty is its noun; عليم: its khabar; خبير: its second khabar; the two clauses headed by إن are resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿قالت الأعراب آمنا قل لم تؤمنوا ولكن قولوا أسلمنا ولما يدخل الإيمان في قلوبكم﴾: قالت الأعراب: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause آمنا is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); the clause لم تؤمنوا is also in the position of accusative as the object of the saying; the wāw is a conjunction particle; لكن: a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal); قولوا: an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause أسلمنا is the object of the saying; the wāw is circumstantial (for the ḥāl); لما: a particle of negation and of the jussive; يدخل: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لما﴾; الإيمان: fāʿil; في قلوبكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يدخل﴾.
﴿وإن تطيعوا الله ورسوله لا يلتكم من أعمالكم شيئا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن: conditional; تطيعوا: the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); رسوله is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the Name of Majesty الله; لا: negative; يلتكم: an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); من أعمالكم: a ḥāl (circumstantial), because it was [originally] an adjective of ﴿شيئًا﴾; شيئًا: a second mafʿūl bihi, or standing in for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
﴿إن الله غفور رحيم﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the Name of Majesty is its noun; غفور: its khabar (predicate); رحيم: its second khabar.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿إنما المؤمنون الذين آمنوا بالله ورسوله ثم لم يرتابوا﴾: إنما: [إنّ] made inoperative (makfūfa) by the preventing [mā] (kāffa); المؤمنون: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذين: khabar (predicate); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position; بالله: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿آمنوا﴾; رسول is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الله, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; ثم: a conjunction particle indicating delay; لم: a particle of negation, of conversion [to past meaning] and of the jussive; يرتابوا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم.
﴿وجاهدوا بأموالهم وأنفسهم في سبيل الله أولئك هم الصادقون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; جاهدوا is conjoined to آمنوا; بأموالهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جاهدوا, and likewise His words في سبيل الله; أولئك: mubtadaʾ; هم: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), or a second mubtadaʾ; الصادقون: the khabar of أولئك, or the khabar of هم, the clause being the khabar of أولئك.

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿قل أتعلمون الله بدينكم والله يعلم ما في السماوات وما في الأرض﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval (inkārī); تعلمون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the Name of Majesty is its object; بدينكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) تعلمون, because it has the sense of "informing"; the wāw is circumstantial (for the ḥāl); الله: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يعلم is the khabar (predicate); ما: a relative noun in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); في السماوات: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, and the ṣila clause has no grammatical position. ﴿ما في الأرض﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿ما في السماوات﴾.
﴿والله بكل شيء عليم﴾: الله: mubtadaʾ; بكل شيء: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿عليم﴾; عليم: khabar.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿يمنون عليك أن أسلموا قل لا تمنوا علي إسلامكم﴾: يمنون: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); عليك: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) يمنون; أن with what falls within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition; قل: an imperative verb; the clause لا تمنوا is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); علي: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تمنوا﴾; إسلامكم is also accusative by removal of the preposition.
﴿بل الله يمن عليكم أن هداكم للإيمان﴾: بل: a particle of digression (iḍrāb) and conjunction; الله: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يمن عليكم is the khabar (predicate); أن with what falls within its scope is also accusative by removal of the preposition; للإيمان: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿هداكم﴾; إن: conditional; كنتم صادقين is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and its apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e. "then He is the One who confers the favour upon you".

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿إن الله يعلم غيب السماوات والأرض﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the Name of Majesty is its noun; يعلم: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as "he"; غيب: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); السماوات: muḍāf ilayhi; الأرض: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to السماوات, genitive; the clause يعلم is the khabar (predicate) of إن.
﴿والله بصير بما تعملون﴾: الله: mubtadaʾ (subject); بصير: khabar; بما تعملون: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بصير﴾.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا: a vocative particle; ﴿أي﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين: an adjective of ﴿أي﴾; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿لا ترفعوا أصواتكم فوق صوت النبي﴾: لا: prohibitive; ترفعوا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); أصواتكم: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فوق: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ترفعوا﴾; صوت النبي: muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿ولا تجهروا له بالقول كجهر بعضكم لبعض أن تحبط أعمالكم وأنتم لا تشعرون﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لا: prohibitive; تجهروا: an imperfect verb, jussive by لا; له: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تجهروا﴾; بالقول: a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to ﴿تجهروا﴾; ﴿كجهر﴾: the kāf is a noun meaning مثل ("like"), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); جهر: muḍāf ilayhi; ﴿لبعض﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to جهر, because it is a maṣdar; أن with what falls within its scope is in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "for fear of [your deeds'] coming to nothing", the fear being on their part; and ﴿لا ترفعوا﴾ and ﴿لا تجهروا﴾ contend for it (tanāzuʿ); أعمالكم: the fāʿil of تحبط; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); أنتم: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause لا تشعرون is the khabar (predicate) of أنتم, and the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

muyesser-irab:3-3.t: ﴿إن الذين يغضون أصواتهم عند رسول الله أولئك الذين امتحن الله قلوبهم للتقوى﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); الذين: its noun; the clause يغضون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿الذين﴾, with no grammatical position. أصواتهم: the object of يغضون; عند رسول الله: the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يغضون﴾; أولئك: mubtadaʾ (subject); الذين: its khabar (predicate); the clause is the khabar of إن; امتحن الله قلوبهم: a verb, its fāʿil (agent) and a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); للتقوى: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿امتحن﴾ with a muḍāf implied, i.e. "for the manifestation of taqwā"; the clause ﴿إن الذين يغضون﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is causal (taʿlīliyya). لهم: a fronted khabar; مغفرة: a postponed mubtadaʾ; أجر عظيم is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to مغفرة; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position, or the khabar of أولئك.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t: ﴿إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات أكثرهم لا يعقلون﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); الذين: its noun; the clause ينادونك is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. من وراء الحجرات: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينادونك﴾; أكثرهم: mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause لا يعقلون is the khabar (predicate) of أكثرهم, and the nominal clause is the khabar of إن.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ولو أنهم صبروا حتى تخرج إليهم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; أن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); ﴿هم﴾: its noun; the clause صبروا is its khabar (predicate); أن with what falls within its scope is interpreted as a maṣdar, the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, its implied form being ثبت ("it were established"), or a mubtadaʾ (subject) that needs no khabar, because the khabar is necessarily omitted after لو and لولا in the view of some; حتى: a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; تخرج: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿صبروا﴾; إليهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to تخرج.
﴿لكان خيرا لهم والله غفور رحيم﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; كان: a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, its noun a pronoun referring to the maṣdar understood from صبروا, i.e. "their patience would have been"; خيرًا: its khabar; لهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خير; الله: mubtadaʾ; غفور: first khabar; رحيم: second khabar.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿يا أيها الذين آمنوا﴾: يا: a vocative particle; ﴿أي﴾: the one addressed (munādā), a specific indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma in the position of accusative (manṣūb); ها is for drawing attention (tanbīh); الذين: an adjective of ﴿أي﴾; the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position.
﴿إن جاءكم فاسق بنبأ﴾: إن: conditional; جاءكم: a past verb in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the kāf is a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); فاسق: a postponed fāʿil (agent); بنبأ: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) جاءكم.
﴿فتبينوا أن تصيبوا قوما بجهالة فتصبحوا على ما فعلتم نادمين﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), because the clause is a request (ṭalabiyya); تبينوا: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; أن تصيبوا: أن with what falls within its scope is in the position of accusative (manṣūb) as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "for fear of your striking"; قومًا: mafʿūl bihi; بجهالة: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil, i.e. "being ignorant"; فتصبحوا: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and تصبحوا is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to تصيبوا; the wāw is the noun of تصبحوا; على ما فعلتم: the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to نادمين; نادمين: the khabar (predicate) of تصبحوا.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿واعلموا أن فيكم رسول الله لو يطيعكم في كثير من الأمر لعنتم﴾: the wāw is a conjunction particle; اعلموا: an imperative verb; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); أن with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا; فيكم: the fronted khabar (predicate) of أن; رسول الله: the postponed noun of إن [Translator's note: so in the source; the particle in the ayah is أنّ]; لو: conditional; the clause يطيعكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun in His words فيكم; في كثير: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يطيعكم﴾; من الأمر: an adjective of كثير; the lām occurs in the apodosis of لو; عنتم: a verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb) of لو.
﴿ولكن الله حبب إليكم الإيمان وزينه في قلوبكم وكره إليكم الكفر والفسوق والعصيان﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; لكن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause حبب is its khabar; إليكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to حبب; الإيمان: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); زينه is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to حبب; في قلوبكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to زينه; وكره إليكم الكفر is conjoined to what precedes.
﴿أولئك هم الراشدون﴾: أولئك: mubtadaʾ (subject); هم: a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl); الراشدون: the khabar of أولئك; or ﴿هم﴾ is a second mubtadaʾ and الراشدون its khabar, the clause ﴿هم الراشدون﴾ being the khabar of أولئك; the clause ﴿أولئك هم الراشدون﴾ is resumptive or parenthetical, and on either view it has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿فضلا﴾: standing in for a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e. تفضَّل فَضْلا ("He bestowed a bounty"), and it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar); or: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
﴿من الله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective of ﴿فضلًا﴾.
﴿ونعمة﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to ﴿فضلًا﴾, accusative.
﴿والله عليم حكيم﴾: the wāw is resumptive; الله: mubtadaʾ (subject); عليم: first khabar (predicate); حكيم: second khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وإن طائفتان من المؤمنين اقتتلوا فأصلحوا بينهما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; إن: conditional; طائفتان: the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb indicated by the verb mentioned after it; من المؤمنين: a naʿt (adjective) of طائفتان; اقتتلوا: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma; the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); أصلحوا: an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; بينهما: an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أصلحوا﴾.
﴿فإن بغت إحداهما على الأخرى فقاتلوا التي تبغي حتى تفيء إلى أمر الله﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن: conditional; بغت: a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters; the tāʾ is for the feminine; إحداهما: the fāʿil of بغت; على الأخرى: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to بغت; the fāʾ is the linking fāʾ; قاتلوا: an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; التي: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause تبغي is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿التي﴾, with no grammatical position. حتى: a particle of limit (ghāya) and of the genitive; تفيء: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied أن after حتى, its fāʿil latent (mustatir), implied as "it" (hiya); the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive (majrūr) by حتى, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قاتلوا; إلى الله: إلى is a preposition and the Name of Majesty a genitive noun, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿تفيء﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the ayah reads ﴿إلى أمر الله﴾].
﴿فإن فاءت فأصلحوا بينهما بالعدل وأقسطوا إن الله يحب المقسطين﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction; إن: conditional; فاءت: a past verb, indeclinable on an implied fatḥa on the alif dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently carried over from بغت above; فاءت is built on an overt fatḥa]; the tāʾ is for the feminine; أصلحوا: an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; بينهما: an adverb attached to ﴿أصلحوا﴾; بالعدل: a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being just"; إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); the Name of Majesty is its noun; the clause ﴿يحب المقسطين﴾ is its khabar (predicate); the clause of إن with what follows it gives the reason for the command, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا: يا is a particle by which one calls; أيّ has ḍamma because it is a single-word vocative (nidāʾ mufrad); ها is for drawing attention; الَّذِينَ is in the position of a nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of أيّ. Some of the Arabs say «اللّذون». آمَنُوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذين». لا تُقَدِّمُوا: jussive by the prohibition. Some grammarians say: jussive by لا because of its resemblance to لم; and some of them say: because of its strength in turning the verb to the future and nothing else.
Several views have been narrated about the occasion of revelation of this verse. Among the soundest of them in chain and the clearest is what ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, who said: Ḥajjāj narrated to us from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abī Mulayka informed me that ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr informed them: A party of riders from Banū Tamīm came to the Prophet ﷺ. Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Appoint al-Qaʿqāʿ ibn Maʿbad as leader." ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Rather, appoint al-Aqraʿ ibn Ḥābis." Abū Bakr said: "You only meant to oppose me." He said: "I did not mean to oppose you." They argued until their voices were raised, and concerning that was revealed: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (1). [Translator's note: the source has «ما أردت إليّ أو إلى خلافي», apparently a corruption of «ما أردتَ إلّا خلافي», which is how it is translated.]
Al-Ḥasan [ibn Muḥammad] said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us, saying: Sufyān ibn Ḥusayn informed us from al-Ḥasan: يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ — he said: do not slaughter [your sacrifices] before the imam. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ — he said: this is in fighting and in the laws of religion: do not decide until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commands. Abū Jaʿfar said: These views are not contradictory; rather, some of them strengthen others, because when these things occurred and the verse was revealed, the people interpreted it according to its apparent sense as disapproval of putting forward speech before the Messenger ﷺ before they had consulted together, and some people interpreted it as prohibiting slaughter before the imam; and this indicates that performing acts of obedience before their time is not permissible — neither advancing prayer nor zakāt.
The reading of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk is «لا تَقَدَّمُوا» [Translator's note: printed in the source identically to the received text; the description that follows (intransitive) requires «لا تَقَدَّمُوا»], and al-Farrāʾ claimed that the meaning in both is the same. Abū Jaʿfar said: Even if the meaning is the same, speaking loosely, there is a difference between them in the language: qaddamtu is transitive, so its implied form is "do not put forward speech and action before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ", whereas taqaddamū is not so, because its implied form is "do not go ahead with speech and action".

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا أَصْواتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ: Ibrāhīm al-Taymī said: Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "O Messenger of Allah, I will not speak to you except like one sharing a secret." Ibn Abī Mulayka said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr said: After the revelation of this verse ʿUmar would not make the Prophet ﷺ hear his speech until he asked him to repeat it. Anas said: Thābit ibn Qays stayed behind in his house and said, "I fear that I am among the people of the Fire", until the Prophet ﷺ sent to him: "You are not among the people of the Fire."
A group of scholars acted on this by disapproving of raising the voice at the grave of the Prophet ﷺ, in the presence of scholars and in mosques, saying: this is the etiquette of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and of His Messenger, upon him be peace. They argued for that from the ḥadīth of al-Barāʾ and others, as was read out to Bakr ibn Sahl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yūsuf, who said: Abū Muʿāwiya informed us from al-Aʿmash, from al-Minhāl, from Zādhān Abū ʿAmr, from al-Barāʾ, who said: We went out with the Prophet ﷺ to the funeral of a man of the Anṣār; we reached the grave, and the niche had not yet been dug. The Prophet ﷺ sat and we sat around him as though birds were on our heads, while the Prophet ﷺ was bent towards the ground. He raised his head and said: "Seek refuge with Allah from the punishment of the grave" — two or three times; and he mentioned the [rest of the] ḥadīth.
In what we have mentioned there are benefits. Among them is the Prophet's ﷺ going out, which indicates that no imam, governor or judge ought to hold back from [fulfilling] obligations because of what he is occupied with.
