In it also is the sitting of the Prophet ﷺ, "and we sat around him as though birds were on our heads", i.e. still, out of reverence for him; this indicates that so ought to behave whoever sits with a scholar or a ruler who must be revered, as ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "He is not of us who does not revere our elder, show mercy to our young, and recognize [the right] of our scholar."
وَلا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ: the kāf is in the position of an accusative, i.e. "a loudness like the loudness of some of you to others". أَنْ تَحْبَطَ أَعْمالُكُمْ: «أن» is in the position of an accusative. Some of the linguists said: i.e. "lest your deeds be nullified"; this is a weak view which, when reflected upon, is known to be an error. The [right] view is what Abū Isḥāq said — it is subtle in Arabic. He said: the meaning is "so that (li-an) [the result is that] your deeds are nullified", and for him it is like فَالْتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهُمْ عَدُوًّا وَحَزَناً [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8] [i.e. the lām of consequence]. وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ: it is said: i.e. you do not perceive that your deeds have been nullified.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أَصْواتَهُمْ: the noun of إنّ. The khabar (predicate) may be أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ لِلتَّقْوى, with «أولئك» a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «الذين» its khabar. It may also be that الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ لِلتَّقْوى is the khabar of إنّ, with «أولئك» a naʿt (adjective) of الذين. And the khabar of إنّ may be لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنادُونَكَ مِنْ وَراءِ الْحُجُراتِ: the noun of «إنّ», and the khabar (predicate) is أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْقِلُونَ. You may also put أكثرهم in the accusative as a badal (substitute) for الذين. Yazīd ibn al-Qaʿqāʿ read «الحُجَرات» with fatḥa on the jīm. Abū ʿUbayd traced it back to its being a plural of a plural, for multiplicity: ḥujra pluralized as ḥujar, then ḥujar pluralized as ḥujarāt. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is contrary to the view of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. Their doctrine is that one says ḥujra and ḥujurāt, ghurfa and ghurufāt, and one may make it fatḥa, saying ḥujarāt and rukabāt, or drop [the vowel], saying ḥujrāt and rukbāt, just as one says ʿaḍud and ʿaḍd. [Translator's note: the source prints these forms unvocalized; the vocalization given follows the well-known doctrine of Sībawayh to which the passage refers.]
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: إنّ الّذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات — Bedouins of Banū Tamīm, among them ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn, who shouted: "Will you not come out to us, O Muḥammad? Come out to us, O Muḥammad!" أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْقِلُونَ [i.e. do not understand] how ugly this is.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ صَبَرُوا, i.e. when calling, حَتَّى تَخْرُجَ إِلَيْهِمْ لَكانَ خَيْراً, i.e. patience would have been better for them; صبروا indicates the implied [subject]. وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ: He forgave them and had mercy on them, because they did not intend contempt by this; it was only bad manners on their part.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: It is [also] read «فتثبّتوا» [instead of فَتَبَيَّنُوا]; they are two well-known readings, except that «فتبيّنوا» is more expressive, because a person may verify carefully (yatathabbat) without [the matter] becoming clear to him. أَنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْماً بِجَهالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا: [فتصبحوا is] conjoined to تصيبوا.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t: The scholars of the people of the Sunna say: the meaning of حَبَّبَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْإِيمانَ is: He granted you success in it, and did acts by which you love faith and find it good; so when they loved it and found it good, the act was attributed to Him. Likewise He did acts by which they came to loathe disbelief, transgression and disobedience. As for the meaning of «حبّب» being "He commanded you to love it", that is wrong from every aspect. Among them: one says only "so-and-so endeared himself to you", i.e. he did deeds for which you loved him. Among them: it is an innovated view whose holder contradicts the text of the Qur'an; He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَما تَوْفِيقِي إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ [Hūd: 88], and from it is His saying اهْدِنَا [al-Fātiḥa: 6] — of exactly this kind. Among them: the text of the verse indicates the opposite of what he said: He, Mighty and Majestic, said أُولئِكَ هُمُ الرَّاشِدُونَ, and there is no disagreement that this refers back to those to whom He endeared faith and made it beautiful in their hearts and made disbelief, transgression and disobedience hateful to them. If the meaning of حبّب were "He commanded them to love it", the disbelievers and the people of disobedience would be included in this — and this is outside the religion. «الراشدون» are those rightly guided to faith who abandoned acts of disobedience. Then He, Mighty and Majestic, made clear that this is a bounty and a blessing from Him, saying, Mighty and Majestic: فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَنِعْمَةً. Abū Isḥāq said: «فضلا» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of bounty. وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ, i.e. knowing of the welfare and benefits of His servants, wise in His acts.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: طائِفَتانِ: nominative by an implied verb, i.e. "and if two parties fight each other". The implied [verb] may also be كان. An implied [verb] is necessary because «إن» is followed only by a verb, since it is for condition. Its apodosis (jawāb) is فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما. فَإِنْ بَغَتْ إِحْداهُما عَلَى الْأُخْرى is also a condition, and the apodosis is فَقاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّى تَفِيءَ إِلى أَمْرِ اللَّهِ, i.e. returns. If you say «تفي» without hamza, its meaning is "becomes abundant". [Translator's note: so in the source; the verb meaning "to be abundant" is usually given as وفى/يفي.] وَأَقْسِطُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: qasaṭa is when one is unjust, and aqsaṭa when one is just — taken from it, i.e. he removed the injustice (al-qusūṭ). In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ: "Those who act justly (al-muqsiṭūn), who are just in their judgement and in what they are put in charge of, are on pulpits of light at the right of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic." [Translator's note: the source begins the ḥadīth with «كثيرا المقسطون», which appears corrupt (the known wording begins «إنّ المقسطين»); the word «كثيرا» is left untranslated.]

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). Since they agreed in religion, they returned to their origin, because they are all children of Adam. The reading of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakra and Ibn Sīrīn is «فأصلحوا بين إخوانكم», and the reading of Yaʿqūb is «فأصلحوا بين إخوتكم». Akh [has the plurals] ikhwa for the lesser number and ikhwān for the greater. وبَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ: between any two Muslims who fight each other, so it has become general.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِنْ قَوْمٍ: jussive by the prohibition. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that some of them used to say to others, "You are not rightly guided", and things like that, mocking them, so this was revealed; and he was from Banū Tamīm. وَلا تَلْمِزُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ: also a prohibition. ʿIkrima said from Ibn ʿAbbās: i.e. let not some of you find fault with others. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: al-lamz in the language is finding fault in someone's presence, and al-hamz in his absence. Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-lamz is with the tongue and the eye: he finds fault with him, fixes his gaze on him, and you point at him disparagingly; al-hamz is only with the tongue, in presence and in absence, mostly in absence. This is a clear explanation. Abū al-ʿAbbās recited, by Ziyād al-Aʿjam [metre: al-basīṭ]:
431- إذا لقيتك تبدي لي مكاشرة ... وإن تغيّبت كنت الهامز اللّمزه
(When I meet you, you show me a broad grin; and if I am absent, you are the backbiter, the fault-finder.)
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: al-lamz is like backbiting. He said: al-nabz is the fixed nickname; he said: and al-munābaza is spreading it and publicizing it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: As for the nickname, there has come a definitive report about it from one who witnessed the revelation and knew about whom the verse was revealed, as was read out to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from Ḥumayd ibn Masʿada, who said: Bishr informed us from Dāwūd, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: Abū Jubayra said: This verse was revealed about us, the Banū Salima. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to Medina, and a man among us had two or three names; he would be called by one of them, and it would be said: "O Messenger of Allah, he gets angry at it." So وَلا تَنابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقابِ was revealed. As for the report of al-Ḍaḥḥāk from Ibn ʿAbbās — "a man would say to another 'O disbeliever, O transgressor', so وَلا تَنابَزُوا بِالْأَلْقابِ was revealed" — the chain of the first is sounder than it; and even if this were sound it would not contradict the first, because the meaning of laqab (nickname), according to what Muḥammad ibn Yazīd and others said, is: whenever it is widespread, a person gets angry at it, the one who says it dislikes meeting its bearer with it, and the one called by it dislikes it, then calling one another by it is forbidden.
بِئْسَ الِاسْمُ الْفُسُوقُ: [الفسوق is] nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the implied form is: "transgression after you have believed — evil is the name". وَمَنْ لَمْ يَتُبْ فَأُولئِكَ هُمُ الظَّالِمُونَ: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said from Ibn ʿAbbās: whoever does not repent of this speech.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t:
يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيراً مِنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ: Ibn ʿAbbās explained wherein the sin lies; he said: that you speak after you suspect; if you hold back, there is no sin. What is clear in this is that the suspicion which is a sin, and forbidden to the one who does it, is to suspect evil of a Muslim whose faults are concealed. As for the suspicion that is recommended, it is that you think good and fine things of him, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: لَوْلا إِذْ سَمِعْتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَالْمُؤْمِناتُ بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ خَيْراً [al-Nūr: 12].
He said: وَلا تَجَسَّسُوا, i.e. do not search out your brother's fault after Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has concealed it for him.
وَلا يَغْتَبْ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضاً: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made clear [what] backbiting [is] on the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ, as was read out to Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥujr, who said: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, saying: al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to us from his father, from Abū Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do you know what backbiting is?" They said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger know best." He said: "That you mention your brother with what he dislikes." It was said: "What if that is [really] in my brother?" He said: "If it is in him, you have backbitten him, and if it is not in him, you have slandered him." This is a ḥadīth whose chain is beyond reproach, and the scholars then proceeded on it. Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn said: If you know that your brother dislikes your saying "how very black his hair is", and then you say it behind his back, you have backbitten him. ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: I said in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ about a woman, "How long her shift is!", and the Prophet ﷺ said: "You have backbitten her, so ask her to absolve you." Abū Naḍra said from Jābir, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Backbiting is worse than fornication, because a man fornicates, then repents, and Allah accepts his repentance; but a man backbites another, then repents, and his repentance is not accepted until [the other] absolves him."
Abū Jaʿfar said: In backbiting there is that for which absolution does not occur, and it is graver, as it is narrated that a man said to Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn: "I have backbitten you, so absolve me." He said: "I do not make lawful what Allah the Exalted has made unlawful." ʿUqayl narrated from Ibn Shihāb that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whatever you would dislike to say to your brother to his face and then say behind his back, you have backbitten him."
أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتاً: this [with doubling, «مَيِّتًا»] is the original; then whoever lightens it says «مَيْتًا». [Translator's note: the source prints the original form as «مَيْتاً» too; the reading with doubling is that of Nāfiʿ.] فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ: al-Kisāʾī said: the meaning is "you dislike it, so you ought to dislike backbiting". Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: i.e. you dislike eating it; so it is construed according to the meaning, like أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ لَكَ صَدْرَكَ وَوَضَعْنا عَنْكَ وِزْرَكَ [al-Sharḥ: 1–2].

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْناكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثى is general, and what follows it is specific, because "peoples" and "tribes" are among the Arabs specifically. إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقاكُمْ: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated — among the Arabs specifically — it was said: [Translator's note: this sentence appears defective in the source, the words «في العرب خاصة» seemingly repeated from above and the rest of the chain lost; translated as written.] "O Messenger of Allah, who is the best of people?" He said: "One whose life is long and whose deeds are good." Durra said: The Prophet ﷺ was asked: "Who is the best of people?" He said: "The one who most enjoins what is right, most forbids what is wrong, most maintains ties of kinship, and is most God-fearing of them." Ibn ʿAbbās said: People have abandoned this verse, إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقاكُمْ, and have said: [honour is] by lineage. Abū Hurayra said: A caller will call on the Day of Resurrection: "I made a lineage and they made a lineage: إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقاكُمْ. Let the God-fearing stand!" and none will stand except those who are so.

nahhas-irab:14-15.t:
قالَتِ الْأَعْرابُ آمَنَّا: Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: this is by treating the group as feminine, i.e. "the group of Bedouins said". قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَلكِنْ قُولُوا أَسْلَمْنا: islām in the language is submission and humbling oneself to the command of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and surrendering to Him; and īmān is affirming the truth of everything that has come from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. When one submits to the command of Allah, Glorified be He, and humbles himself to Him, he is one who affirms; and when he affirms, he is a believer; and whoever is of this description is a Muslim and a believer. However, islām has another usage, namely yielding out of fear of being killed.
وَإِنْ تُطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ لا يَلِتْكُمْ مِنْ أَعْمالِكُمْ شَيْئاً: this is the reading of most people, and on it the authority is established. Abū ʿAmr and al-Aʿraj read «لا يألتكم», which contradicts the text of the codex (al-sawād), except that whoever reads so argues from the agreement of all on وَما أَلَتْناهُمْ [al-Ṭūr: 21]. What is to be said about this is that they are two known, well-known dialect forms; and since that is so, following the text of the codex is preferable.

nahhas-irab:16-16.t: قُلْ أَتُعَلِّمُونَ اللَّهَ بِدِينِكُمْ: for intensiveness, from «تعلمون».

nahhas-irab:17-17.t: يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ أَسْلَمُوا: «أن» is in the position of an accusative, in the meaning "they count their Islam as a favour to you"; the implied form may also be "bi-an", then the bāʾ was dropped. بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ هَداكُمْ, i.e. "bi-an" or "li-an"; then the particle was dropped and the verb became transitive [i.e. accusative by removal of the preposition].

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: وَاللَّهُ بَصِيرٌ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), i.e. knowing of it; and when He knows it, He will recompense it.

semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {لاَ تُقَدِّمُواْ}: the majority read it with ḍamma on the tāʾ, fatḥa on the qāf and the dāl doubled with kasra, and there are two views about it. The first: that it is transitive and its object is omitted, either for brevity, as in their saying "he gives and withholds", {وَكُلُواْ واشربوا} [al-Baqara: 187], or by way of abbreviation because it is indicated, that is: "do not put forward what is not fitting." The second: that it is intransitive, like «وَجَّه» and «تَوَجَّه», supported by the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḍaḥḥāk «لا تَقَدَّمُوا» with fatḥa in the three letters; the original is «لا تَتَقَدَّمُوْا», one of the two tāʾs being dropped. Some Meccans read «لا تَّقَدَّمُوْا» likewise, / except with the tāʾ doubled, like the tāʾs of al-Bazzī. That which is reached by the preposition in these two readings is also omitted, that is: "do not advance to any matter." «لا تُقْدِموا» was also read, with ḍamma on the tāʾ and kasra on the dāl, from «أَقْدَمَ», that is: "do not venture upon anything."

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {أَن تَحْبَطَ}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. The matter is one of tanāzuʿ (competing operators), because each of His sayings «لا تَرْفَعوا» and {لاَ تَجْهَرُواْ لَهُ} demands it in meaning; so it is governed by the second according to the Basrans' preference, and by the first according to the Kufans. The first is sounder because of the omission from the first, that is: «لأَنْ تحبطَ». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "It is the lām of consequence (ṣayrūra)", and there is no need for that. {وَأَنتُمْ لاَ تَشْعُرُونَ} is a ḥāl.

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {أولئك}: «أولئك» may be a mubtadaʾ with «الذين» as its khabar, the sentence being the khabar of «إنَّ», and «لهم مغفرةٌ» another sentence: either resumptive, which is the apparent sense, or a ḥāl clause. It is also possible that «الذين امتحنَ» is an adjective of «أولئك», or a badal from it, or an explicative apposition, with «لهم مغفرةٌ» a predicative sentence. It is also possible that «لهم» alone is the khabar and «مغفرةٌ» is its agent.

semin-durr:4-4.t: His saying: {مِن وَرَآءِ}: «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the range. In al-Zamakhsharī's discussion there is something that denies that «مِنْ» can mean both the beginning and the end of the range. He said: "because one and the same thing cannot be both the starting point and the end point of the action." Some people affirmed this and claimed that it indicates the beginning and end of the action in a single direction, as in «أَخَذْتُ الدرهمَ من الكيس» ("I took the dirham from the purse"). The majority read «الحُجُرات» with two ḍammas. Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba read it with fatḥa. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it with sukūn. These are three dialectal forms, verified earlier in al-Baqara at His saying {فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ} [al-Baqara: 17]. «الحُجْرَةُ» is a «فُعْلَة» in the sense of «مَفْعولة», like «غُرْفة» in the sense of «مَغْروفة».

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ صَبَرُواْ}: the like of it has been given earlier. al-Zamakhsharī made it an agent of an implied verb, that is: "had their patience been established", and made the ism of «كان» a pronoun returning to this agent. It has already been said that Sībawayh's school is that it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and then the ism of «كان» is a pronoun returning to their patience, understood from the verb.

semin-durr:6-6.t: His saying: {أَن تُصِيببُواْ}: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, like His saying {أَن تَحْبَطَ} [al-Ḥujurāt: 2].

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {لَوْ يُطِيعُكُمْ}: it may be a ḥāl, either from the genitive pronoun in «فيكم», or from the latent nominative pronoun in «فيكم», since [the other] leads to a discord in the composition. What he said is not apparent; rather, the resumptive is also clear. He used the imperfect after «لو» to indicate that it was in their wish that his action continue according to what they fabricate.
His saying: {ولكن الله}: the istidrāk (rectification) here is by meaning, not by wording, because the one to whom faith was made beloved differs in description from the one mentioned earlier.
And His saying: {أولئك هُمُ} is an iltifāt from address to the third person.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {فَضْلاً}: it may be accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi. There are two views about what governs it. The first: His saying {ولكن الله حَبَّبَ إِلَيْكُمُ}, and on this what lies between them, His saying {أولئك هُمُ الراشدون}, is parenthetical. The second: that it is «الراشدون». On this, how is it permissible with a different agent, since the agent of right guidance is not the agent of bounty? al-Zamakhsharī answered: "Since right guidance came to be an expression for making beloved, adorning and making disliked, all attributed to His names, right guidance became as if it were His act." He also allowed it to be accusative by an implied verb, that is: "that took place" or "that was". The Shaykh said: "This is not one of the places for implying «كان»", and he considered his first statement to be Muʿtazilism. It is not so, because he meant the verb attributed to its agent in wording; otherwise the verified position is that all acts are created by Allah the Exalted, even if al-Zamakhsharī does not agree with that. It may also be accusative as a maṣdar of emphasis for the content of the preceding sentence, because it too is bounty; but Ibn ʿAṭiyya made it a maṣdar of self-emphasis. al-Ḥūfī allowed it to be accusative as ḥāl, which is not apparent, the implied form being: "bestowing favour, granting grace", or "possessed of bounty and favour".

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {اقتتلوا}: it returns to the individuals of the two groups, as in His saying {هذان خَصْمَانِ اختصموا} [al-Ḥajj: 19], and in «بينهما» it follows the wording. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «اقْتتلَتا», taking the wording into account. Zayd ibn ʿAlī and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read «اقتتلا» also, except that he made the verb masculine considering the two parties, or because it is a figurative feminine.
His saying: {حتى تفياء}: the majority read it with hamza, from «فاء يَفيء», that is, he returned, like «جاء يجيْء». al-Zuhrī read it with a yāʾ with fatḥa, like the imperfect of «وَفَى»; this is in the dialect of those who shorten and say «جا، يَجي» without hamza, and then he put fatḥa on the yāʾ because it became the final letter of declension. /

semin-durr:10-10.t:
His saying: {بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ}: the majority read the dual. Zayd ibn Thābit, ʿAbd Allāh, al-Ḥasan, Ḥammād ibn Salama and Ibn Sīrīn read «إخوانِكم» in the plural on the pattern «فِعْلان». It has already been said that «الإِخوان» predominates for friendship and «الإِخْوَة» for kinship, and it may be reversed, as in this verse. From Abū ʿAmr and a group «إخْوَتِكم» with tāʾ (from above) is reported. All three readings are also reported from Abū ʿAmr.
The disagreement about «القوم» has been given earlier. al-Zamakhsharī made it here a plural of «قائم», saying: "like «صَوْم» and «زَوْر», plurals of «صائم» and «زائر»", but «فَعْل» is not among the patterns of the broken plural except according to al-Akhfash, as in «رَكْب» and «صَحْب».
Ubayy and ʿAbd Allāh read «عَسَوْا» and «عَسَيْنَ», treating it as a defective verb (i.e. as a regular verb with suffixes), which is the dialect of Tamīm. The majority read it in the Ḥijāzī dialect. al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj read «ولا تَلْمُزوا» with ḍamma. «اللَّمْزُ» is by speech and otherwise, and «الهَمْزُ» with the tongue only.
His saying: {وَلاَ تَنَابَزُواْ}: «التنابُزُ» is a «تفاعُل» from «النَّبْزِ», which is calling by nickname. And «النَّزْبُ» is transposed from it, given the rarity of this and the frequency of that; one says «تنابَزُوا» and «تنازَبُوا» when they call each other by a bad nickname. Its origin is from raising, as if the nickname raises its bearer so that he is seen. «اللَّقَبُ» is what indicates the lowliness of the one named, like «قُفَّة» and «بَطَّة», or his eminence, like «الصِّدِّيق», «عتيق», «الفاروق», «أسدِ الله» and «أسدِ رسوله». It has, together with the name and the kunya, rulings which I have mentioned in grammar.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {إِثْمٌ}: al-Zamakhsharī made its hamza a substitute for a wāw, saying: "because it «يَثِمُ» the deeds, that is, it breaks them." This is not conceded; rather that is another root. «ولا تَجَسَّسوا»: «التجسُّسُ» is following up; from it come «الجاسوس» (spy) and «الجَسَّاسَةُ». «جَواسُّ الإِنسان» and «حواسُّه» are his faculties of perception. al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ and Ibn Sīrīn read it here with ḥāʾ.
His saying: {مَيْتاً}: accusative as ḥāl from «لحم» or «أخيه». The disagreement about «مَيْتا» was given earlier.
His saying: {فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ}: al-Farrāʾ said: "Its implied form is: 'then you have disliked it, so do not do it.'" Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "That to which it is conjoined is omitted, its implied form being: 'That was presented to you and you disliked it', the meaning being: 'It is presented to you and you dislike it.' It is also said: 'If that is established with you, then you dislike it.'" It is also said: it is a report with the sense of a command, as in their saying "May a man who did good fear Allah; he will be rewarded for it." Abū Ḥaywa and al-Jaḥdarī read «فَكُرِّهْتُموه» with ḍamma on the kāf and the rāʾ doubled, made transitive by doubling to a second [object], unlike His first saying {وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيْكُمُ الكفر} [verse 7], which, though doubled, takes only one object because it includes the sense of «بَغَّض» (to make hateful).

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوباً وَقَبَآئِلَ}: «الشُّعوب» is the plural of «شَعْب», which is the highest of the levels of lineage. The levels of lineage the Arabs have are six: the shaʿb, the qabīla, the ʿimāra, the baṭn, the fakhidh and the faṣīla, each entering into the one before: the faṣīla enters into the fakhidh and the fakhidh into the baṭn. Some people added after the fakhidh the ʿashīra, making seven. The shaʿb was called shaʿb because the tribes branch (tashaʿʿub) out of it, and the tribes were so called because of their facing one another (taqābul), likened to the qabāʾil of the head, which are opposing pieces. It is also said: the shuʿūb are among the non-Arabs, the qabāʾil among the Arabs, and the asbāṭ among the Children of Israel. It is also said: the shaʿb is the more distant lineage and the qabīla the nearer. And he recited:
4086 - قبائلُ مِنْ شُعوبٍ ليس فيهِمْ ... كريمٌ قد يُعَدُّ ولا نَجيبُ
(Tribes from peoples among whom there is no noble man worth counting, nor any distinguished one.)
The attribution to the shaʿb is «شَعوبيَّة» with fatḥa on the shīn; they are a people who hate the Arabs.
His saying: {لتعارفوا}: the majority read it with the tāʾ light; the original is «لتتعارفوا», one tāʾ being dropped. al-Bazzī reads it with the tāʾ doubled. That was given earlier in al-Baqara. The lām is attached to «جَعَلْناكم». al-Aʿmash read it with two tāʾs, which is the original that al-Bazzī assimilated and the majority dropped one of. Ibn ʿAbbās read «لِتَعْرِفُوا», the imperfect of «عَرَفَ». The majority read «إنَّ أكْرَمَكم» with kasra. Ibn ʿAbbās read it with fatḥa: if you make the lām the lām of command, which is remote, it becomes clear that His saying «أنَّ أَكْرَمَكم» with fatḥa is the object of knowing: He commanded them to know that. If you make it the lām of cause, it is not apparent that it be an object, because He did not make them peoples and tribes so that they know that; so the object ought to be made omitted and the lām for cause, that is: "so that you may know the truth, because the most honoured of you..."

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ}: this sentence is resumptive; the Exalted informs of that. al-Zamakhsharī made it a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قولوا». The discussion of «لَمَّا», what it indicates and the difference between it and «لم» has been given earlier. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: after His saying «لم تؤمنوا» it resembles repetition without a new benefit; I say: it is not so, for the benefit of His saying «لم تؤمنوا» is to give the lie to their claim, and «لَمَّا يَدْخُل» fixes a time limit for what they were commanded to say." Then he said: "What is in «لَمَّا» of the sense of expectation is evidence that these later believed." The Shaykh said: "I do not know in what respect what is negated by «لَمَّا» occurs afterwards." I say: because it negates «قد فَعَلَ», and «قد» is for expectation.
His saying: {لاَ يَلِتْكُمْ}: Abū ʿAmr read «لا يَأْلِتْكُمْ» with hamza, from «أَلَتَه يَأْلُتُهُ» with fatḥa in the past and kasra or ḍamma in the imperfect, and al-Sūsī replaces the hamza with alif according to his principle. The others read «يَلِتْكم», from «لاته يَليتُه» like «باعه يَبيعه», which is the Ḥijāzī dialect; the first is the dialect of Ghaṭafān and Asad. It is also said that it is from «وَلَتَه يَلِتُه» like «وَعَده يَعِدُه»; so the omitted letter on the first view is the ʿayn of the word and its pattern is «يَفِلْكم», and on the second its fāʾ and its pattern is «يَعِلْكم». One also says «ألاتَه يُليته» / like «أَباعه يُبِيعه», and «آلتَهَ يُؤْلِتُه» like «آمَنَ يُؤْمِنُ». All of these are dialectal forms with the meaning: he diminished him of his due. al-Ḥuṭayʾa said: 4087 - أَبْلِغْ سَراةَ بني سعدٍ مُغَلْغَلَةً ... جَهْدَ الرسالةِ لا أَلْتاً ولا كَذِباً
(Convey to the nobles of Banū Saʿd a message carried far, the utmost of messages, with no diminishing and no falsehood.)
And Ruʾba said:
4088 - وليلةٍ ذاتِ ندىً سَرَيْتُ ... ولم يَلِتْني عن سُراها ليتُ
(Many a night full of dew I journeyed, and nothing held me back from travelling it.)
that is: it did not prevent me or restrain me.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {أَتُعَلِّمُونَ}: this is derived by doubling from «عَلِمْتُ به» in the sense of "I was aware of it", hence it is transitive to one object by itself and to another with the bāʾ.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {أَنْ أَسْلَمُواْ}: two views are permissible. The first: that it is a mafʿūl bihi, because «يَمُنُّون» is taken to include the sense of «يَعْتَدُّون» (they count as a favour), as if it were said: "they count their Islam as a favour upon you, reproaching you with it"; hence he made the direct object explicit in His saying {لاَّ تَمُنُّواْ عَلَيَّ إِسْلاَمَكُمْ}, that is: "do not count your Islam as a favour upon me." Thus the Shaykh argued from this. There is room for doubt in it, for one may say: we do not concede that «إسلامَكم» is accusative as a direct object; rather it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi, as it is permissible in the position of «أَنْ أَسْلَموا», which is the second view, that is: "they reproach you because they submitted"; likewise in His saying {لاَّ تَمُنُّواْ عَلَيَّ إِسْلاَمَكُمْ}, the conditions of the accusative are present, and the mafʿūl li-ajlihi, when annexed, may equally be genitive with a preposition or accusative.
And His saying: {أَنْ هَداكُمْ} is like «أن أَسْلَموا». Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «إذ هَداكم» with «إذ» in place of «أَنْ», which gives the sense of cause. The apodosis of the condition is implied, that is: "then it is He who confers favour upon you, not you upon Him or upon me."

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {والله بَصِيرٌ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ}: Ibn Kathīr read it in the third person, looking to His saying «يَمُنُّون» and what follows it; the others in the second person, looking to His saying {لاَّ تَمُنُّواْ عَلَيَّ إِسْلاَمَكُمْ} to the end.

ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ (١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا تُقَدِّمُوا): the mafʿūl (object) is omitted, i.e. "do not put forward what is not fitting".
It is also read with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the dāl, i.e. "do not go ahead" (تَتَقَدَّمُوا).

ukberi-tibyan:10-10.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّمَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ إِخْوَةٌ فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُرْحَمُونَ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَيْنَ أَخَوَيْكُمْ): (read) with the dual and with the plural, and the meaning is understood.

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِنَ الظَّنِّ إِنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إِثْمٌ وَلَا تَجَسَّسُوا وَلَا يَغْتَبْ بَعْضُكُمْ بَعْضًا أَيُحِبُّ أَحَدُكُمْ أَنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أَخِيهِ مَيْتًا فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَوَّابٌ رَحِيمٌ (١٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَيْتًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from اللَّحْم, or from أَخِيهِ.
(فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ): what it is conjoined to is omitted, its implied form being: "that was presented to you, and you loathed it".
The meaning is: "it is presented to you, and you loathe it".
It is also said: "if that is established in your view, then you loathe it".

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ ذَكَرٍ وَأُنْثَى وَجَعَلْنَاكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَائِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوا إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أَتْقَاكُمْ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ (١٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِتَعَارَفُوا), i.e. "so that you may know one another".
It is also read لِتَعْرِفُوا (إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ) with fatḥa on the hamza (i.e. أَنَّ), and أَنَّ together with what it governs is the mafʿūl (object).

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (قَالَتِ الْأَعْرَابُ آمَنَّا قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا وَلَكِنْ قُولُوا أَسْلَمْنَا وَلَمَّا يَدْخُلِ الْإِيمَانُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَإِنْ تُطِيعُوا اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ لَا يَلِتْكُمْ مِنْ أَعْمَالِكُمْ شَيْئًا إِنَّ اللَّهَ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (١٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَلِتْكُمْ): it is read with a hamza after the yāʾ, its past tense being أَلَتَ.
It is also read without hamza, its past tense being لَاتَ يَلِيتُ. They are two dialects, and both mean "to diminish".
There is a third dialect in it: يُلْيِتُ. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لَا تَرْفَعُوا أَصْوَاتَكُمْ فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ وَلَا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالْقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ أَنْ تَحْبَطَ أَعْمَالُكُمْ وَأَنْتُمْ لَا تَشْعُرُونَ (٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تَحْبَطَ), i.e. "for fear that (your deeds) be nullified", or "so that (they) be nullified", taking the lām as the lām of outcome (lām al-ʿāqiba). It is also said: "lest (they) be nullified" (لِئَلَّا تَحْبَطَ).

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أَصْوَاتَهُمْ عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهُمْ لِلتَّقْوَى لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ وَأَجْرٌ عَظِيمٌ (٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أُولَئِكَ) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ» is its khabar (predicate). And (لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ) is another clause.
«الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ» may also be an adjective (ṣifa) of أُولَئِكَ, with «لَهُمْ مَغْفِرَةٌ» as the khabar; and the whole is the khabar of إِنَّ.

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنْ جَاءَكُمْ فَاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أَنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهَالَةٍ فَتُصْبِحُوا عَلَى مَا فَعَلْتُمْ نَادِمِينَ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تُصِيبُوا) is like «أَنْ تَحْبَطَ».

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ فِيكُمْ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ يُطِيعُكُمْ فِي كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الْأَمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْإِيمَانَ وَزَيَّنَهُ فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ وَكَرَّهَ إِلَيْكُمُ الْكُفْرَ وَالْفُسُوقَ وَالْعِصْيَانَ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الرَّاشِدُونَ (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَوْ يُطِيعُكُمْ) is resumptive. It may also be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), what governs it being the (implied) settledness (al-istiqrār). That is permissible only because it may occur as an adjective of an indefinite noun, as when you say: مَرَرْتُ بِرَجُلٍ لَوْ كَلَّمْتُهُ لَكَلَّمَنِي ("I passed by a man who, had I spoken to him, would have spoken to me"), i.e. ready for that.

ukberi-tibyan:8-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَضْلًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَنِعْمَةً وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ (٨) وَإِنْ طَائِفَتَانِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا فَإِنْ بَغَتْ إِحْدَاهُمَا عَلَى الْأُخْرَى فَقَاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي حَتَّى تَفِيءَ إِلَى أَمْرِ اللَّهِ فَإِنْ فَاءَتْ فَأَصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُمَا بِالْعَدْلِ وَأَقْسِطُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُقْسِطِينَ (٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَضْلًا) is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the meaning of what preceded, because His making faith attractive is a bounty; or it is a mafʿūl (object). And (طَائِفَتَانِ) is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb. And (اقْتَتَلُوا) is plural according to the individuals of the two groups.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ḥujurāt
﷽
﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُقَدِّمُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيِ اللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ﴾: it has also been read "لا تَقَدَّمُوا", with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the dāl. The meaning is: "when you are commanded to do something, do not do it before the time at which you were commanded to do it." It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that a man slaughtered on the Day of Sacrifice before the prayer of the Sacrifice, and so went ahead before the time; and Allah made known that that is not permissible. In this there is proof that it is not permissible to perform an obligatory act before its time, nor a voluntary act before its time, among those which the Sunna has brought. In this there is also proof that paying zakāt early, before its time, ought not to be permissible. As for what is related, «that the Prophet ﷺ took some of the zakāt in advance from al-ʿAbbās», I do not know of anyone among those who permitted paying zakāt early who argued with anything except this ḥadīth. This, if it is sound, is of two kinds: one of them is that it is a special case; the other is that the need had become severe, so that there was necessity to take the zakāt in advance. The consensus is that giving it at its time is what is right, and it is what is better, if Allah wills. Whoever reads "لا تَقَدَّمُوا", its meaning is like the meaning of ﴿لا تُقَدِّمُوا﴾.

zajjaj:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تَرْفَعُوا أصْواتَكم فَوْقَ صَوْتِ النَّبِيِّ ولا تَجْهَرُوا لَهُ بِالقَوْلِ كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded them to revere His Prophet, upon him be peace, to lower their voices, to address him with calm and dignity, and to give him precedence in address — that being what they used to do in honouring their chiefs and their great men. The meaning of ﴿كَجَهْرِ بَعْضِكم لِبَعْضٍ﴾ is: do not put him in the position that you hold with one another, so that you say: "يا مُحَمَّدُ" (O Muḥammad); address him by his prophethood, with calm and reverence.
His saying: ﴿أنْ تَحْبَطَ أعْمالُكُمْ﴾: its meaning is: "do not do that, lest your deeds come to nothing", and the meaning is: "so that your deeds do not come to nothing". So the meaning is the meaning of the lām in "أنْ", and this lām is the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra), like the lām in His saying: ﴿فالتَقَطَهُ آلُ فِرْعَوْنَ لِيَكُونَ لَهم عَدُوًّا وحَزَنًا﴾ [al-Qaṣaṣ: 8], the meaning being: "the family of Pharaoh picked him up, so that their affair came to that" — not that they intended it to come to that; but it was in what had been decreed in Allah's prior knowledge that the cause of that outcome was their picking him up. Likewise: "do not raise your voices, lest that become a cause for your deeds coming to nothing". ﴿وَأنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ﴾: this is a notification that the affair of the Prophet ﷺ ought to be exalted and honoured with the utmost honour, and that something may be done regarding the Prophet ﷺ without one being aware of it, and that becomes ruinous for the one who does it or says it. For that reason some of the jurists said: whoever says: "إنَّ زِرَّ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ ﷺ وسِخٌ" (the button of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is dirty), intending to belittle him, must be killed. This is the doctrine of Mālik and his followers.

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يَغُضُّونَ أصْواتَهم عِنْدَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ امْتَحَنَ اللَّهُ قُلُوبَهم لِلتَّقْوى﴾: He made their hearts pure; and "هُمْ" comes out according to the explanation of the true sense of the language. [Translator's note: the source reads «و”هُمْ“»; «وهو» ("and it") may be intended.] The meaning is: Allah tested their hearts and found them sincere, as you say: "قَدِ امْتَحَنْتُ هَذا الذَّهَبَ، وهَذِهِ الفِضَّةَ" (I have tested this gold and this silver); its interpretation is: I have tried them by melting them until I purified the gold and the silver, and so I knew the true nature of each of them.

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ يُنادُونَكَ مِن وراءِ الحُجُراتِ﴾: it is read with ḍamma on the ḥāʾ and the jīm, and "اَلْحُجَراتِ" with fatḥa on the jīm. "اَلْحُجْراتِ", with sukūn on the jīm, is permissible in the language, but I do not know anyone who read it with sukūn. We have explained this plural earlier in the book. The singular of al-ḥujurāt is "حُجْرَةٌ" (chamber). It is possible that "اَلْحُجُراتُ" is the plural of "حُجَرٌ", [as in] "حُجُراتٌ"; but the better view is that "اَلْحُجُراتُ" is the plural of "حُجْرَةٌ", and that the fatḥa was allowed as a substitute for the ḍamma because of the heaviness of two ḍammas. These were people of Banū Tamīm who came to the Prophet ﷺ and called to him from behind the chambers. There is a lengthy account about them in the tafsīr (exegesis); its gist is that they came to vie in boasting with the Prophet, and that they did not meet him in the manner due to him, upon him be peace.

zajjaj:5-5.t: He said: ﴿وَلَوْ أنَّهم صَبَرُوا حَتّى تَخْرُجَ إلَيْهِمْ لَكانَ خَيْرًا لَهم واللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾, that is: whoever repents after this deed, Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إنْ جاءَكم فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ فَتَبَيَّنُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا﴾ — and it is read: "فَتَثَبَّتُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا" (then make sure, lest you harm) — ﴿قَوْمًا بِجَهالَةٍ﴾: It has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that it was revealed on account of al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba. «The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent him as a collector to gather the alms of Banū al-Muṣṭaliq, and between him and them there was iḥna, that is: enmity. When news of him reached them, as he had set out toward them, they said to one another: You know what is between us and this man, so withhold your alms from him. That reached him, and he returned to the Prophet ﷺ and told him that they had withheld the alms from him, that they had apostatised, and that they had prepared weapons for war. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ dispatched Khālid ibn al-Walīd with an army, and instructed him to descend on their territory by night: if he saw what indicated their persisting in Islam — the call to prayer, prayer and night vigil — he should refrain from fighting them and ask them for their alms. When Khālid reached them by night, he heard the call to prayer and saw them praying and keeping vigil, and they said to him: We had thought the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding the alms slow in coming; and they handed them over to him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿إنْ جاءَكم فاسِقٌ بِنَبَإٍ﴾», that is: with a report, ﴿فَتَبَيَّنُوا أنْ تُصِيبُوا قَوْمًا بِجَهالَةٍ﴾, that is: out of aversion to harming a people in ignorance. This is proof that it is not permissible to accept a report from a fāsiq (a person of evident sinfulness), even if he makes it clear, and that it is permissible to accept the report of a trustworthy person (thiqa). "اَلثِّقَةُ" is one against whom false testimony has not been established, who is not known for sinfulness, and who has not been flogged in a ḥadd punishment, and who in addition has sound discernment.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿واعْلَمُوا أنَّ فِيكم رَسُولَ اللَّهِ لَوْ يُطِيعُكم في كَثِيرٍ مِنَ الأمْرِ لَعَنِتُّمْ﴾, that is: had he obeyed the like of this informant, who told him what had no basis, you would have fallen into ʿanat; "اَلْعَنَتُ" is corruption and ruin. ﴿وَلَكِنَّ اللَّهَ حَبَّبَ إلَيْكُمُ الإيمانَ﴾: by this the sincere believers are meant. ﴿وَزَيَّنَهُ في قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾: "فِي قُلُوبِكُمْ" admits two aspects. One of them is that He guided them to it by decisive, clear proofs and the miraculous signs which the Prophet ﷺ brought; the second is that He made it seem fair in their hearts by granting them success (tawfīq).
﴿وَكَرَّهَ إلَيْكُمُ الكُفْرَ والفُسُوقَ والعِصْيانَ﴾: that too is His making clear to them what is against them in disbelief, and His granting them success if they avoid it.
His saying: ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الرّاشِدُونَ﴾, that is: these whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has granted success by making faith beloved to them and disbelief hateful — those are the rightly guided.

zajjaj:8-8.t: ﴿فَضْلا مِنَ اللَّهِ ونِعْمَةً﴾ is accusative (manṣūb), a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). The meaning is: "Allah did that for you as a bounty from Allah and a favour", that is: for the sake of bounty and favour. Were it outside the Qur'an, "فَضْلٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ ونِعْمَةٌ" (nominative) would be permissible, the meaning being: "that is a bounty from Allah and a favour".

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنْ طائِفَتانِ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ اقْتَتَلُوا فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما فَإنْ بَغَتْ إحْداهُما عَلى الأُخْرى فَقاتِلُوا الَّتِي تَبْغِي﴾: the transgressing party is the one that deviates from the truth and from what the leaders of the Muslims and their community are upon. ﴿حَتّى تَفِيءَ إلى أمْرِ اللَّهِ﴾: until it returns to the command of Allah. ﴿فَإنْ فاءَتْ﴾: then if it returns, ﴿فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَهُما بِالعَدْلِ وأقْسِطُوا﴾, that is: and be just; ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ المُقْسِطِينَ﴾. It was said that this was revealed on account of two groups of the Anṣār between whom there was fighting, and that was not with swords or weapons; it has come in the tafsīr (exegesis) that there was fighting between them with hands and sandals, and throwing of stones at one another.

zajjaj:10-10.t: ﴿إنَّما المُؤْمِنُونَ إخْوَةٌ فَأصْلِحُوا بَيْنَ أخَوَيْكُمْ﴾: it is also read "بَيْنَ إخْوانِكُمْ", "بَيْنَ إخْواتِكُمْ" and "بَيْنَ أخْوَتِكُمْ". Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that religion unites them, and that they are brothers when they agree in their religion; so in agreeing in religion they returned to the root of lineage, because they are [descended] from Adam and Eve. Had their religions differed, they would have parted in lineage, even if originally they are from one father and one mother. Do you not see that the believing child does not inherit from the disbelieving father, nor does the believing close relative inherit from his disbelieving kinsman?

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا يَسْخَرْ قَوْمٌ مِن قَوْمٍ﴾ — the verse: it may be that the one mocked is better than those who mock, and likewise it may be that the women who are mocked are better than the women who mock. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, forbade believing men to mock believing men, and believing women to mock believing women. ﴿وَلا تَلْمِزُوا أنْفُسَكُمْ﴾: "اَللَّمْزُ" and "اَلْهَمْزُ" are faulting and disparaging a person. Allah made known that their faulting one another clings to them: the fault of the one faulted clings to the one who faults. ﴿وَلا تَنابَزُوا بِالألْقابِ﴾: "اَلنَّبْزُ" and "اَللَّقَبُ" have one meaning: a Muslim should not call someone who was a Jew or a Christian and then accepted Islam by a nickname reproaching him for having been a Christian or a Jew. ﴿بِئْسَ الاسْمُ الفُسُوقُ بَعْدَ الإيمانِ﴾, that is: evil is the name, that he should say to him: "يا يَهُودِيُّ" (O Jew) and "يا نَصْرانِيُّ" (O Christian), when he has believed. It may also apply to every nickname a person dislikes, because the believer ought to address his brother only by the names dearest to him.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اجْتَنِبُوا كَثِيرًا مِنَ الظَّنِّ إنَّ بَعْضَ الظَّنِّ إثْمٌ﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded avoiding much suspicion, namely that you think evil of people of goodness, when we know that what has appeared from him is good. As for people of evil and sinfulness, we may think of them the like of what has appeared from them.
His saying: ﴿وَلا يَغْتَبْ بَعْضُكم بَعْضًا﴾: "اَلْغَيْبَةُ" (backbiting) is (that a person is mentioned behind his back with evil, even if the evil is in him; as for mentioning him with what is not in him, that is "اَلْبَهْتُ" and "اَلْبُهْتانُ" (slander), (thus it has come from the Prophet ﷺ.
[Translator's note: the parentheses in the source are not closed.]
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أيُحِبُّ أحَدُكم أنْ يَأْكُلَ لَحْمَ أخِيهِ مَيْتًا﴾ — "مَيِّتًا" is also permissible. Its interpretation is that your mentioning with evil someone who is not present with you is like eating his flesh while he is dead and does not feel it. Likewise you say of the backbiter: "فُلانٌ يَأْكُلُ لُحُومَ النّاسِ" (So-and-so eats people's flesh).
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ﴾ — and it is read: "وَكَرِهْتُمُوهُ" — its interpretation is: "just as you hate to eat his flesh dead, likewise avoid mentioning him with evil in his absence."

zajjaj:13-13.t: His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النّاسُ إنّا خَلَقْناكم مِن ذَكَرٍ وأُنْثى﴾: We created you from Adam and Eve; all of you are children of one father and one mother, and to them you go back. ﴿وَجَعَلْناكم شُعُوبًا وقَبائِلَ لِتَعارَفُوا﴾: "اَلشَّعْبُ" (people, nation) is greater than the tribe. That is: He did not make you nations and tribes so that you might boast against one another; We made you so only that you might know one another. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known to them that the highest of them in rank with Him is the most God-fearing of them, and said: ﴿إنَّ أكْرَمَكم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أتْقاكُمْ﴾. Had it been read "أنَّ أكْرَمَكم عِنْدَ اللَّهِ أتْقاكُمْ" (with fatḥa on the hamza), that would be permissible, in the sense of: "We made you nations so that you might know one another, because the noblest of you with Allah is the most God-fearing of you."

zajjaj:14-14.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قالَتِ الأعْرابُ آمَنّا قُلْ لَمْ تُؤْمِنُوا ولَكِنْ قُولُوا أسْلَمْنا ولَمّا يَدْخُلِ الإيمانُ في قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾: this is a place that people need to understand: where the believer (muʾmin) is distinguished from the Muslim, and where the two are equal. Islam is the outward display of submission and acceptance of what the Prophet ﷺ brought, and by that blood is protected. If, along with that outward display, there is conviction and affirmation by the heart, that is faith (īmān), and whoever is so described is a believer and a Muslim. He is the one who believes in Allah and His Messenger without doubt or uncertainty, who holds that performing the obligations is binding upon him and that striving with his person and his wealth is binding upon him, no doubt entering him in that: he is the believer, and he is the Muslim in truth, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنَّما المُؤْمِنُونَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِاللَّهِ ورَسُولِهِ ثُمَّ لَمْ يَرْتابُوا وجاهَدُوا بِأمْوالِهِمْ وأنْفُسِهِمْ في سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الصّادِقُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 15], that is: when they say "we are believers", they are the truthful. As for one who outwardly displays acceptance of the Law and submits in order to ward off what is hateful, he is outwardly a Muslim while inwardly not affirming; that is the one who says "أسْلَمْتُ" (I have submitted), because faith requires that its possessor be one who affirms, since your saying "آمَنتُ بِكَذا وكَذا" (I believed in such-and-such) means "I affirmed it as true". So Allah excluded these people from faith and said: ﴿وَلَمّا يَدْخُلِ الإيمانُ في قُلُوبِكُمْ﴾, that is: you have not affirmed; you only submitted to seek refuge from being killed. So the believer conceals within him affirmation equal to what he displays; the Muslim complete in Islam is the one who displays obedience and in addition believes in it; and the Muslim who displayed Islam to seek refuge is not a believer in reality, except that his outward legal status is the status of the Muslims.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿يَمُنُّونَ عَلَيْكَ أنْ أسْلَمُوا قُلْ لا تَمُنُّوا عَلَيَّ إسْلامَكم بَلِ اللَّهُ يَمُنُّ عَلَيْكم أنْ هَداكم لِلإيمانِ إنْ كُنْتُمْ صادِقِينَ﴾: it was said that this was revealed about the hypocrites: so know that if you are truthful, then you have submitted, and the favour upon you belongs to Allah, for His bringing you out of misguidance into guidance. It has also been said that it was revealed about others than the hypocrites, about some people among the Muslims who said: We believed, we emigrated, we did and we accomplished, and so they reminded the Messenger of Allah of that as a favour. The more likely — and Allah knows best — is that it concerns some people among the hypocrites.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنْ تُطِيعُوا اللَّهَ ورَسُولَهُ لا يَلِتْكم مِن أعْمالِكم شَيْئًا﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 14]: it is also read "لا يَأْلَتْكُمْ". Whoever reads "يَأْلَتْكُمْ", his proof is ﴿وَما ألَتْناهم مِن عَمَلِهِمْ مِن شَيْءٍ﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 21], whose meaning is "and We did not diminish them"; likewise "لا يَأْلَتْكُمْ": He will not diminish you. Whoever reads ﴿لا يَلِتْكُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 14], it is from "لاتَ، يَلِيتُ"; one says "لاتَهُ، يَلِيتُهُ" and "ألاتَهُ، يُلِيتُهُ" when one diminishes him as well. The meaning of the two is the same, I mean "يَأْلَتْكُمْ" and "يَلِتْكُمْ". The reading ﴿لا يَلِتْكُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 14] is more common, and the other — I mean "يَأْلَتْكُمْ" — is good and eloquent, and its proof in the Qur'an is as we have described.
